candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Surface Coating of Plastic Parts and Products

criteria.criterion: If you apply a material to plastic parts or products (including adhesives) then that activity is within the surface coating source category covered by this subpart.

If the affected source uses 378 liters (100 gallons) per year or more of coatings that contain hazardous air pollutants and the facility is a major source (≥9.07 Mg/yr (10 tpy) of any single HAP or ≥22.68 Mg/yr (25 tpy) of combined HAP), then the source is subject to this subpart.
If the specific surface-coating or coating operation meets any of the exclusions listed in §63.4481(c)(1) through (17), then that coating operation is not subject to this subpart.

If the material applied is an "adhesive" as defined (a chemical substance applied for the purpose of bonding two surfaces together), then it counts as a coating/covered material under this subpart unless it falls into the specific exceptions listed in the adhesive definition.

If the applied material leaves coating solids (a dry film), you must determine organic HAP content per mass of coating solids and compare to the emission limits in §63.4490 using the procedures in §63.4541; if the applied material leaves no coating solids you must still classify the material (coating, thinner/additive, or cleaning material) because thinners/additives/cleaning materials are included in emissions calculations and applicability.

If you elect the compliant-material option then no coating used may have an organic HAP content exceeding the applicable emission limits and no thinner, additive, or cleaning material used may contain organic HAP as determined under §63.4541.

If you do not use the compliant-material option, then you must include all coatings, thinners/additives, and cleaning materials in the emission-rate calculations (with or without add-on controls) and follow the procedures in §63.4561 (emission rate with add-on controls) or §63.4551 (emission rate without add-on controls) to demonstrate compliance with the emission limits in §63.4490.

If you add six new lines and those changes meet the definition of a new or reconstructed affected source per §63.4482(c) (construction after Dec 4, 2002 or new coating equipment/subcategory not previously performed), then the new/modified lines are subject as new or reconstructed affected source(s).

checklist: Describe exactly what the methylene-chloride step does (is it applied to bond parts = adhesive; is it intended to leave a coating/film; is it surface preparation or cleaning?).
Collect material data sheets and manufacturer's formulation data for the methylene chloride material(s): organic HAP content, volatile matter, and solids content.
Determine whether the methylene-chloride application leaves any coating solids/dry film on the substrate (yes/no and measured solids fraction).

Measure or estimate annual consumption (volume and mass) of the methylene-chloride material and all other coatings, thinners, additives, and cleaning materials used in the plastic parts operations (gallons per year and liters per month).
Determine whether total coatings that contain HAP used at the affected source are ≥378 L (100 gal)/yr.
Evaluate facility-level HAP potential to emit (tons per year) to establish whether the facility is a major source (≥10 tpy single HAP or ≥25 tpy total HAP).
Confirm whether the solvent-welding step is performed as part of a coating operation as defined (is it 'application of coating to a substrate' or only a separate bonding operation?).
Check whether the material or product fits any specific exclusion in §63.4481(c)(1)-(17) (e.g., research lab, facility-wide no-organic-HAP use, specific product categories listed).
If treating the material as an adhesive, verify whether it falls into the adhesive exceptions (products used on humans/animals, adhesive tape, contact paper, or adhesive on an inert substrate).

If planning to use the compliant-material option, verify each material's organic HAP content vs. the applicable emission limits in §63.4490 and confirm thinners/additives/cleaning materials contain no organic HAP per §63.4541.

If planning to use emission-rate options, compile monthly records of volumes, densities, mass fraction organic HAP, and coating solids for all relevant materials to run the calculations in §63.4561 and §63.4551.
Document whether the six added lines constitute 'new' or 'reconstructed' per §63.4482(c) and retain records of installation dates and equipment changes.

Assemble process descriptions, photographs or line diagrams showing application method (wipe, brush, spray, dip), capture/enclosure arrangements, and whether emissions are routed to any control devices.

judge_text: {"score": 1, "reason": "The answer includes the key point that MeCl used to bond parts is an 'adhesive'/coating (cites §63.4581/§63.4481) but does not capture the EPA's decisive rationale that because the solvent welding leaves no coating solids the §63.4490 metric (lb HAP per lb solids) cannot be determined and therefore the subpart was not applied; the criteria instead describe procedures for classifying materials and doing emissions calculations even when no solids, so only some EPA reasons are reflected."}

candidates.title: General Provisions (40 CFR part 63, subpart A)

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate a new affected source that is subject to Subpart FFFFFF, then the General Provisions in 40 CFR part 63, subpart A apply to that affected source.

candidates.title: Area Source NESHAP for Secondary Copper Smelting

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate a new secondary copper smelter that is an area source of HAP emissions (new affected source = constructed or reconstructed on or after October 6, 2006), then you are subject to this subpart.

If your facility processes copper scrap in a blast furnace and converter or uses another pyrometallurgical purification process to produce anode copper from copper scrap, then it meets the definition of 'secondary copper smelter' for this subpart.

If your facility merely melts recycled copper scrap or copper alloy scrap to produce ingots or for direct use in a manufacturing process (not to produce anode copper via pyrometallurgical purification), then it is not a 'secondary copper smelter' and is not subject to this subpart.
If you are a research and development facility as defined in CAA section 112(c)(7), then this subpart does not apply to you.

candidates.title: Area Source NESHAP for Aluminum, Copper, and Other Nonferrous Foundries

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate a copper foundry that melts copper or copper-based alloys and pours molten copper into molds to manufacture complex copper castings and you are an area source meeting the material or production criteria in §63.11544(a)(1)–(4), then you are subject to this subpart.

If your melting operation uses material containing copper foundry HAP (e.g., materials containing lead or nickel ≥0.1% by weight or manganese ≥1.0% by weight), then your foundry is subject to this subpart.

If your annual metal melt production (for an existing source) or annual metal melt capacity (for a new source) of copper and other nonferrous metals is at least 600 tons per year, then you are subject to this subpart.

If you are a primary or secondary metal producer that casts molten copper to produce simple shapes such as sows, ingots, bars, rods, billets, or anode copper, then you are not a 'copper foundry' for purposes of this subpart (and the foundry provisions would not apply as a 'copper foundry').
If you are a research or laboratory facility as defined in section 112(c)(7) of the Clean Air Act, then this subpart does not apply to you.

candidates.title: Area Source NESHAP for Secondary Nonferrous Metals Processing

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate a secondary nonferrous metals processing facility (as defined in §63.11472) that is an area source of HAP emissions, then you are subject to this subpart.
If you are not a secondary nonferrous metals processing facility, then this subpart does not apply.

checklist: Do you process copper scrap using a pyrometallurgical purification process (e.g., smelting/oxidation/reduction) to produce anode copper that is shipped off site for electrolytic refining?
Does the facility cast molten copper into anodes (anode copper) rather than pouring molten copper into molds to make complex castings?
Is the facility classified as a 'secondary copper smelter' under the definition (processes scrap via blast furnace/converter or other pyrometallurgical purification to produce anode copper)?
Is the source an area source of HAPs (facility-wide potential HAP emissions below major-source thresholds per §63.2/state permitting determinations)?
Was construction or reconstruction of the affected source commenced on or after October 6, 2006 (i.e., is it a 'new' affected source for Subpart FFFFFF)?

Do you purchase or use scrap or other materials that contain copper foundry HAP (lead or nickel ≥0.1% by weight, or manganese ≥1.0% by weight) such that the material meets the 'material containing copper foundry HAP' definition?
What is your annual metal melt production (existing) or annual metal melt capacity (new) of copper and other nonferrous metals (tons per year) — is it ≥600 tpy?

Do you operate as a primary or secondary metal producer that produces simple cast shapes or anode copper (sows, ingots, bars, rods, billets, or anode copper) — i.e., not a 'foundry' for Subpart ZZZZZZ?
Does your facility meet the definition of a 'secondary nonferrous metals processing facility' (verify activities against the definition in §63.11472, if applicable)?
Is the facility a research or laboratory facility as defined in CAA section 112(c)(7)?

judge_text: {"score": 2, "reason": "EPA's key reasons are (1) the anode furnace is a pyrometallurgical purification producing anode copper (meets the §63.11158 definition of secondary copper smelter) and (2) the unit is a new area source covered by §63.11153(a)-(b). Those two points are explicitly captured in the provided criteria and checklist (citations to §63.11158 and §63.11153(a)-(b) present)." }

candidates.title: National Perchloroethylene Air Emission Standards for Dry Cleaning Facilities

criteria.criterion: If you are the owner or operator of a dry cleaning facility that uses perchloroethylene (PCE), then Subpart M applies to that facility.
If a dry cleaning system is located in a building with a residence, then after December 21, 2020 the owner or operator shall eliminate any emission of PCE from that dry cleaning system.

If a dry cleaning system commenced construction or reconstruction on or after December 21, 2005 but before July 13, 2006 and is located in a building with a residence, then the owner or operator must comply with the specific vapor-barrier, refrigerated condenser/carbon adsorber, and weekly inspection requirements in §63.322(o)(5)(ii)(A)–(C) in addition to other applicable requirements.

If the total yearly PCE consumption of the dry cleaning facility is less than 530 liters (140 gallons) per year for the conditions in paragraph (d), then certain existing dry-to-dry facilities (and specified equipment) are exempt from many provisions of §§63.322, 63.323, and 63.324 as described in §63.320(d).

If the total yearly PCE consumption of the dry cleaning facility is less than 760 liters (200 gallons) per year for the conditions in paragraph (e), then certain existing transfer-only facilities are exempt from many provisions of §§63.322, 63.323, and 63.324 as described in §63.320(e).

If the facility emits or has the potential to emit more than 9.1 megagrams per year (10 tons/yr) of PCE, or meets the consumption thresholds in §63.320(g) (>8,000 L for dry-to-dry-only or >6,800 L for transfer/mixed), then the facility is a major source and is subject to the major-source provisions of this subpart.
If you operate a coin-operated dry cleaning machine, then that coin-operated machine is exempt from the requirements of this subpart.

If the dry cleaning facility is located in a building with a residence, even if the residence is vacant at the time of notification, then the owner or operator had to report that fact in the notification of compliance status as specified by §63.324(f).

candidates.title: General Provisions

criteria.criterion: If a relevant standard under section 112 of the Act applies to an affected source, then the owner or operator of that affected source must comply with the requirements in §63.6 unless an extension or exemption has been granted.
If the affected source is new or reconstructed, then compliance dates and obligations for new/reconstructed sources are set out in §63.6(b).
If the affected source is existing, then the compliance dates for existing sources are established in §63.6(c).

If an affected source is subject to a relevant standard, then at all times the owner or operator must operate and maintain the source and associated control and monitoring equipment consistent with safety and good air pollution control practices and must develop a written startup, shutdown, and malfunction (SSM) plan as required by §63.6(e)(1)(i) and §63.6(e)(3).

candidates.title: General requirements for complying with Subpart EEEE

criteria.criterion: If you are subject to Subpart EEEE, then you must be in compliance with the emission limitations, operating limits, and work practice standards in that subpart at all times when the identified equipment is in operation and must operate and maintain the affected source according to §63.6(e)(1)(i) (unless otherwise specified by that subpart).
If you are subject to Subpart EEEE, then Table 12 to that subpart shows which parts of the General Provisions (40 CFR part 63, §§63.1–63.15) apply to you.

checklist: Do you use perchloroethylene (PCE) at this facility (any PCE purchases/receipts)? (§63.320(a))
Is the shop located in the same building as a residence (dwelling where people reside) as defined in §63.321? (note: the rule counts a residence even if vacant) (§63.321; §63.324(f)(3))
Was the residence/upper apartment occupied short-term (<180 days) or is it a dwelling (check §63.321 Residence definition)? (§63.321)

What is the date of construction or reconstruction of the dry cleaning machine(s) (commencement date) and/or date of installation or relocation of any used machine? (to compare to Dec 9, 1991; Dec 21, 2005; July 27, 2006; July 13, 2006) (§63.320(b),(c))
Is the machine a dry-to-dry machine or a transfer machine system? (affects thresholds and applicable provisions) (§63.321 definition; §63.320(d),(e),(g))
Was the machine installed (or reconstructed) after December 21, 2005 or after July 27, 2006? (triggers different requirements in §63.322(o)) (§63.320(b),(2),(3))

What is the facility's total yearly PCE consumption calculated per §63.323(d) (sum of purchases for previous 12 months)? (to determine area vs major and exemption thresholds) (§63.323(d); §63.320(d),(e),(g))
Does the facility emit or have the potential to emit >9.1 Mg/yr (10 ton/yr) PCE (or meet the numeric consumption thresholds for major source)? (§63.320(g))
Is the dry cleaning machine coin-operated (customer-operated)? If yes, it may be exempt. (§63.320(j))

Has the facility submitted the required notifications and compliance-status reports (initial notification, compliance status, and the July 28, 2008 notification items including whether located in a building with a residence)? (check §63.324(a),(b),(f))

If the system is in a building with a residence, can you eliminate emissions by the methods in §63.322(o)(5)(ii)(A)–(C) (vapor-barrier enclosure exhausted to carbon adsorber, refrigerated condenser + non-vented carbon adsorber prior to door opening, weekly leak inspections with halogenated hydrocarbon detector)? (§63.322(o)(5)(ii))
Do you maintain required records on-site for 5 years (PCE purchase receipts, monthly volumes, yearly consumption calc, inspection/repair logs, monitoring results) per §63.324(d)–(e)? (§63.324(d),(e))

Is Subpart EEEE potentially applicable at this site (if yes, check Table 12 to Subpart EEEE to determine which General Provisions apply) and confirm operation/maintenance/SSM obligations per §63.2350 and §63.2398? (40 CFR 63.2350; 63.2398)

judge_text: {"score": 1, "reason": "The answer includes the key citations that a co-located residence counts even if vacant (cites §63.321 and §63.324(f)(3)) and the Dec. 21, 2020 elimination requirement (§63.322(o)(5)(i)), but it does not explicitly state the EPA’s point that the post-2020 prohibition applies so long as the PCE machine remains in the building regardless of whether the machine is currently operating/idle."}

candidates.title: Metal Fabrication and Finishing Area Sources

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate an area source that is primarily engaged in the operations in one of the nine metal fabrication and finishing source categories listed in § 63.11514(a)(1)–(9), then you are subject to this subpart.

If you perform machining, dry abrasive blasting, dry grinding/dry polishing with machines, spray painting, or welding operations that use materials that contain or have the potential to emit metal fabrication and finishing HAP (MFHAP) as defined in § 63.11522, then the affected-source provisions of this subpart apply to those operations.
If your facility is a research or laboratory facility as defined by the CAA, then this subpart does not apply to that facility.
If the operations are tool or equipment repair, facility maintenance, or quality control activities as defined in § 63.11522, then this subpart does not apply to those activities.

If the operations are performed on-site at specified federal installations (Armed Forces, Coast Guard, National Guard, NASA, or NNSA) or the operations produce military munitions or equipment used directly and exclusively to transport military munitions, then this subpart does not apply.

candidates.title: Plating and Polishing Area Sources

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate a plating and polishing facility that performs one or more listed processes (non-chromium electroplating, electroless plating, other non‑electrolytic metal coating processes, thermal spraying, dry mechanical polishing after plating, electroforming, or electropolishing), is an area source, and uses or emits plating-and-polishing metal HAP (compounds of cadmium, chromium, lead, manganese, or nickel), then you are subject to this subpart.
If a specific process unit is subject to the requirements of 40 CFR part 63, subpart N (chromium electroplating/anodizing), then that process unit is not covered by this subpart.

If a process unit is research and development, used strictly for educational purposes, conducted to repair surfaces or equipment, used for dry mechanical polishing solely to restore the original finish, or uses process materials that contain plating-and-polishing metal HAP below the threshold concentrations (cadmium, chromium, lead, or nickel <0.1% by weight; manganese <1.0% by weight) as used, then that process unit is not subject to this subpart.

checklist: Determine whether your facility is an "area source" (potential to emit any single HAP < 10 tpy and total HAP < 25 tpy) for the site and document PTE calculations for the last 12 months.

Determine whether the facility is "primarily engaged" (≥50% of production by appropriate unit of measure over the previous continuous 12 months) in one of the nine metal fabrication and finishing source categories in 63.11514(a)(1)–(9); document the production basis and calculation.

List all on-site operations and processes (e.g., machining, dry abrasive blasting, dry grinding/dry polishing with machines, spray painting, welding, electroplating, electroless plating, thermal spraying, electroforming, electropolishing, dry mechanical polishing) and identify which are routine vs. quality-control/repair/maintenance/R&D/educational.

For each process that could emit metal HAP, collect Material Safety Data Sheets (MSDS)/formulation or supplier data and verify metal content against MFHAP thresholds (cadmium, chromium, lead, nickel ≥0.1% by weight; manganese ≥1.0% by weight) to determine whether the material "contains MFHAP."

For spray painting: verify whether paints are spray-applied (and therefore governed by spray-painting definitions) and whether spray booths/rooms or spray equipment meet the subpart's descriptions and requirements.
For welding: determine if welding rods containing MFHAP are used and quantify welding-rod usage on a rolling 12‑month basis (to compare to 2,000 lb/yr thresholds for additional requirements).

For abrasive blasting and dry grinding/polishing: identify whether blasting/grinding is "totally enclosed and unvented" or vented, and whether capture and filtration controls are used and documented per manufacturer's specifications.

For plating/polishing: identify each tank/process unit (including pH and cyanide use where applicable), whether any unit is subject to subpart N (chromium electroplating), and whether any flash/short‑term electroplating or continuous tanks are present.

Document whether any operations occur on installations owned/operated by the Armed Forces, NASA, or NNSA, or involve manufacture of military munitions or equipment used exclusively for transporting munitions.

Compile records needed to support applicability determinations and future compliance (production share calculations, MSDS/formulation data, manufacturer's specifications for capture/control devices, records demonstrating repair/maintenance/QC exclusions, and PTE documentation).

candidates.title: Lime Manufacturing Plants

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate a lime manufacturing plant (an establishment that uses a lime kiln to produce lime product by calcination of limestone, dolomite, shells, or other calcareous substances) that is a major source of HAP, then this subpart applies to the plant's lime kiln(s), associated cooler(s), and processed stone handling operations located at that LMP.

If the material you calcine in the kiln is not limestone/dolomite/shells but is another calcareous substance (for example, calcium carbonate–rich lime mud), then that calcination may still constitute manufacture of lime product and be subject to this subpart.

If your plant is not a major source of HAP (i.e., does not emit or have the potential to emit ≥9.07 Mg/yr (10 tpy) of any single HAP or ≥22.68 Mg/yr (25 tpy) of any combination of HAP), then this subpart does not apply to the plant.

If the LMP is located at a kraft pulp mill, soda pulp mill, sulfite pulp mill, beet sugar manufacturing plant, or only processes sludge containing calcium carbonate from water softening processes, then this subpart does not apply to that LMP.

If construction or reconstruction of a lime kiln (and, for PM purposes, its associated cooler) began after December 20, 2002 and you met the applicability criteria in §63.7081 at that time, then that kiln is a 'new lime kiln' for PM; and if construction or reconstruction began after January 5, 2023 and you met the applicability criteria in §63.7081 at that time, then that kiln is a 'new lime kiln' for HCl, mercury, organic HAP, and D/F.

If you wish to claim that your LMP is an area source (i.e., not a major source) for applicability determinations, then you must measure hydrogen chloride emissions from all lime kilns (subject to permitting authority discretion for idled or essentially identical kilns) using the specified test methods before claiming area source status.

candidates.title: General Provisions

criteria.criterion: If you are subject to subpart AAAAA, then the General Provisions in §§63.1 through 63.16 apply to you as indicated in Table 9 to subpart AAAAA, and where there is overlap subpart AAAAA takes precedence.

checklist: Determine whether the plant is a major source of HAP (calculate actual and potential emissions: any single HAP ≥ 9.07 Mg/yr (10 tpy) or combined HAPs ≥ 22.68 Mg/yr (25 tpy)).
Confirm whether the kiln performs calcination to produce a lime product (calcium oxide, CaO with MgO, or dead-burned dolomite) rather than an unrelated thermal process.

Characterize the kiln feedstock (provide laboratory analysis or documented composition showing whether the material is limestone, dolomite, shells, or other calcareous material such as calcium carbonate–rich lime mud and report % CaCO3 or equivalent).
Document the purpose and fate of the lime produced (on-site reuse only vs. sale/distribution) and whether production meets the definition of 'lime produced' under the subpart.

Verify whether the facility is collocated at one of the listed excluded facility types (kraft pulp mill, soda pulp mill, sulfite pulp mill, beet sugar manufacturing plant) or only processes water softening sludge.

Record construction and reconstruction dates for the kiln and cooler to determine 'new' vs 'existing' status (compare to Dec 20, 2002 and Jan 5, 2023 / July 16, 2024 as referenced in subpart provisions).
Identify whether the kiln has an associated lime cooler, processed stone handling operations, and whether those emission units are part of the plant site subject to the subpart.

If claiming area source status, determine and plan HCl testing for all kilns (or obtain permitting authority agreement for testing fewer kilns) using EPA Method 320, EPA Method 321, or approved ASTM alternatives per §63.7142 and document test dates and results.

Assemble records of control equipment and capture systems (baghouses, fabric filters, DSI, etc.) and routine monitoring/OM&M plans in case subpart AAAAA applies and to prepare for initial compliance demonstrations and notifications.

judge_text: {"score":2,"reason":"The answer includes the key EPA points: it states that calcining calcareous lime mud can meet the subpart AAAAA definition of a lime manufacturing plant, it lists the regulatory exclusions (pulp mills, beet sugar plants, water‑softening sludge) and it explicitly addresses that lime need not be sold (on‑site reuse), matching the EPA Notes."}

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants for Stationary Reciprocating Internal Combustion Engines (RICE)

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate existing spark-ignition 4SLB or 4SRB stationary RICE with a site rating of more than 500 HP located at an area source of HAP, then the requirements in Table 2d and the operating limitations in Table 2b of this subpart apply to you.

If an existing non-emergency 4SLB or 4SRB stationary RICE with a site rating of more than 500 HP located at an area source met the definition of remote stationary RICE in §63.6675 on the engine's initial compliance date (October 19, 2013), then it is considered a remote stationary RICE under this subpart and subject to the provisions that apply to remote stationary RICE.

If an existing non-emergency 4SLB or 4SRB stationary RICE with a site rating of more than 500 HP located at an area source is not a remote stationary RICE and is operated more than 24 hours per calendar year, then the initial compliance demonstration for that engine must be conducted as specified in §63.6630(e) (including the specified performance test runs and measurement requirements).

If you claim remote stationary RICE status for existing non-emergency SI 4SLB or 4SRB engines that met the remote definition on October 19, 2013, then you must evaluate the engine's remote status every 12 months and keep records of the initial and annual status evaluations; if an evaluation shows the engine no longer meets the remote definition you must comply with all requirements for non-remote engines within 1 year of the evaluation.

If you own or operate an existing stationary RICE located at an area source of HAP, then you must conduct any initial performance test or other initial compliance demonstration required in Tables 4 and 5 within 180 days after the compliance date specified in §63.6595.

candidates.title: General Provisions

criteria.criterion: If an affected source becomes subject to a relevant standard under this part, then the owner or operator must submit the initial notification required by this section (e.g., the written notification that the source is subject) not later than 120 calendar days after the effective date of the relevant standard or within 120 days after the source becomes subject.

If a State requires a notice that contains all the information required in a notification listed in this section, then the owner or operator may submit a copy of the notice sent to the State to the Administrator to satisfy the notification requirements in this section.

If you are required to submit a Notification of Compliance Status for a relevant compliance demonstration, then you must submit that notification before the close of business on the 60th day following completion of the relevant compliance demonstration activity (or before the 30th day if the initial compliance demonstration did not include a performance test as provided in the relevant standard).

checklist: Confirm each engine is spark-ignition, four-stroke lean-burn (4SLB) and non-emergency.
Confirm each engine's site-rated brake horsepower (site rating = 800 HP).
Confirm the facility is an area source of HAP (not a major source).
Confirm each engine is an existing engine (construction/reconstruction commenced before the applicable date in §63.6590 for area-source existing engines).

Determine whether each engine met the definition of remote stationary RICE per 40 CFR 63.6675 on the initial compliance date (October 19, 2013) — e.g., verify building counts and distances within 0.25 mile and absence of >4-story buildings as applicable.
Maintain or locate records of the initial and subsequent annual remote-status evaluations (required if claiming remote status).
Determine annual hours of operation for each engine (verify whether >24 hours/year).

Verify whether any initial performance test(s) required by this subpart have already been conducted, and if so whether any such test is less than 2 years old and was conducted using the same methods and accepted by the Administrator per §63.6612(b).

If no prior acceptable performance test exists and testing is required, note the deadline to conduct initial performance tests (within 180 days after the compliance date per §63.6612(a) and the compliance dates in §63.6595).
Verify whether initial notifications and Notification(s) of Compliance Status required under §§63.6645 and 63.9 have been submitted to the State or EPA (including dates and copies).

If claiming remote/work-practice compliance instead of performance testing, verify you satisfied the remote-definition timing requirement (met remote definition on Oct 19, 2013) and have the required annual evaluations and records per §63.6603(f).

judge_text: {"score":1,"reason":"The answer includes the key regulatory basis for annual remote-status evaluation and recordkeeping (40 CFR 63.6603(f)/63.6675), but it does not capture the EPA note that no separate notification of remote status is required for existing engines (the answer instead lists notification requirements generally) nor does it mention the conditional approval being for the delegated state (Utah DAQ). Thus some but not all key reasons are present."}

candidates.title: National emission limitations and management practices for Gasoline Dispensing Facilities (GDF)

criteria.criterion: if the facility is a gasoline dispensing facility (GDF) located at an area source, then the affected source includes each gasoline storage tank and is subject to this subpart

if the fuel in a tank meets the definition of gasoline (Reid vapor pressure ≥ 27.6 kPa) and is used as fuel for internal combustion engines, then that tank is a gasoline storage tank for purposes of this subpart
if the GDF's monthly throughput of gasoline is less than 10,000 gallons, then the facility must comply with the requirements in § 63.11116
if the GDF's monthly throughput of gasoline is 10,000 gallons or more, then the facility must comply with the control requirements in § 63.11117
if the GDF's monthly throughput of gasoline is 100,000 gallons or more, then the facility must comply with the additional requirements in § 63.11118

if a gasoline storage tank has a capacity of less than 250 gallons, then it is not required to comply with the submerged-fill requirements in § 63.11117(b) and must comply only with the requirements in § 63.11116
if equipment is used only for the refueling (dispensing) of motor vehicles, then that dispensing equipment is not covered by this subpart (storage tanks remain addressed separately)

if the affected source is subject to this subpart only because it loads gasoline into fuel tanks other than those in motor vehicles, then different recordkeeping start dates and compliance dates specified in § 63.11111(e) and § 63.11113(f) apply

candidates.title: Area-source standards for bulk gasoline terminals, pipeline breakout stations, pipeline pumping stations, and bulk gasoline plants

criteria.criterion: if you own or operate a bulk gasoline terminal, pipeline breakout station, pipeline pumping station, or bulk gasoline plant as identified in § 63.11081(a)(1)–(4), then you are subject to this subpart

if gasoline storage tanks are located at an affected source identified in § 63.11081(a) and those tanks are used only for dispensing gasoline in a manner consistent with tanks located at a gasoline dispensing facility (GDF), then those tanks are not subject to this subpart and must comply with subpart CCCCCC

if an affected source's throughput ever exceeds the applicable throughput threshold for bulk gasoline terminals or bulk gasoline plants, then the affected source will remain subject to requirements for sources above the threshold even if throughput later falls below the threshold

checklist: Verify the fuel type in each tank (is the tank storing gasoline as defined by Reid vapor pressure ≥ 27.6 kPa, or diesel/other fuel?)
Record the capacity of each tank (gallons) and date of installation or construction
Confirm whether the tanks are fixed stationary storage tanks at a single physical location treated as one GDF, or portable/other configurations

Determine whether the tanks are used to dispense fuel directly into motor vehicle fuel tanks (on-site company vehicles) or used for other purposes (e.g., loading cargo tanks or non‑motor-vehicle engines)

Calculate monthly throughput for the GDF by summing gasoline loaded into or dispensed from all gasoline storage tanks at the single GDF over the current day plus the previous 364 days and dividing by 12 (to determine if <10,000; ≥10,000; or ≥100,000 gallons thresholds are met)
Check whether any tanks are <250 gallons (or <2,000 gallons and constructed before Jan 10, 2008) for submerged-fill or control exemptions under § 63.11117(c)

Confirm whether the tanks are part of a bulk gasoline terminal/plant/pipeline station (subject to subpart BBBBBB) or are used only in a manner consistent with a GDF (in which case CCCCCC applies per § 63.11081(c))
Determine whether the equipment in question is ‘equipment used for the refueling of motor vehicles’ (dispensing equipment) versus covered storage/tank components
Check construction/startup dates relevant to applicable compliance and recordkeeping dates (e.g., before/after Jan 10, 2008; dates in § 63.11113 and § 63.11111(e))
Identify any enforceable State/local/Tribal rules or permit requirements (e.g., requiring submerged fill) that might affect notification obligations or allow election to comply under those rules
Verify existing recordkeeping and availability of throughput records (records must be available within 24 hours upon request per § 63.11116(b) / § 63.11117(d))

Determine whether you must submit notifications (Initial Notification/Notification of Compliance Status) based on the throughput category and applicable sections (§ 63.11124 and § 63.11117/§ 63.11118 criteria)

judge_text: {"score":2, "reason":"Both key reasons from the EPA notes are represented: the answer cites that subpart CCCCCC covers gasoline storage tanks at an area-source GDF used to dispense into motor vehicles (criteria and checklist address GDF status, tanks used for vehicle refueling, and applicable citations), and it separately identifies fuel-type eligibility using 40 CFR 63.11132 (so a diesel tank would not be ‘‘gasoline’’ and thus not subject)." }

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants for Portland Cement Manufacturing (Subpart LLL)

criteria.criterion: If the coal mill uses kiln exhaust gases in its process (i.e., is an in-line coal mill), then the coal mill is an affected source under this subpart (treated as part of the kiln for determining applicable emissions limits).

If the coal mill is not an in-line coal mill (for example it uses a heat source other than the kiln or uses clinker cooler exhaust), then it is not an in-line coal mill and is not treated as part of the kiln under the definition in this subpart.

If kiln gases are diverted through an in-line coal mill and the coal mill exhausts through a separate stack, then the coal mill's PM emissions must be included with the kiln (combined) to determine compliance with the kiln PM emission limit.

If the kiln exhaust and coal mill exhaust are combined and sent to the same PM control device as a single stream, then the commingled exhaust may meet an alternative (flow-weighted) PM emission limit calculated using the equations in §63.1343(b).

If the coal mill (as part of the kiln affected source) is subject to the PM limits in Table 1 of §63.1343, then initial PM compliance must be demonstrated by Method 5 or 5I performance testing and continuous compliance must be demonstrated using a PM continuous parametric monitoring system (PM CPMS) with annual performance tests to set and reassess the site-specific operating limit.

If the coal mill and kiln exhaust through separate stacks but are both part of the affected kiln system, then the required PM performance tests for the kiln and the coal mill/alkali bypass must be conducted simultaneously and the combined PM emission rate computed for each test run.
If subject to the PM performance test, then the three-test-run requirements, minimum sample volumes, and other performance test conditions in §63.1349(b)(1)(vi) must be met when using Method 5 or 5I.

If the coal mill exhaust is counted toward kiln emission limits expressed as lb/ton clinker, then exhaust flow rates and clinker production (and, where required, continuous measurement of exhaust flow rate) must be available to compute flow-weighted or mass-based emissions (including use of maximum design exhaust flow if allowed under testing provisions).

If a PM CPMS is used, then it must provide a 4–20 mA or digital output, have an operating range to read from zero to three times the allowable emission limit, and be used to demonstrate continuous compliance using a 30 kiln operating day rolling average with the site-specific operating limit set from performance testing.

If the kiln is classified as an existing or new kiln per §63.1343 Table 1, then the applicable numeric PM limits (e.g., existing kiln 0.07 lb/ton clinker; new kiln 0.02 lb/ton clinker) apply to the kiln emission source (including inline coal mills treated as part of the kiln) unless the alternative commingled limit is used.

checklist: Does the coal mill use kiln exhaust gases (i.e., is it an in-line coal mill) or does it use a separate heat source or clinker-cooler exhaust? (verify per 40 CFR 63.1341)
Is the coal mill exhaust discharged through its own separate stack or combined/commingled with the kiln/clinker cooler/alkali bypass into a single control device? (verify flow routing and stacks)
Is the kiln a 'new' source (construction/reconstruction after May 6, 2009) or an 'existing' source for application of numeric PM limits in Table 1 of §63.1343? (verify construction date and status)

If coal mill exhaust is separate, can you and will you perform simultaneous PM performance testing of kiln and coal mill and compute combined PM (plan for simultaneous Method 5/5I testing)? (see 40 CFR 63.1349(b)(1)(viii))

If using the alternative commingled PM limit, what are the exhaust flow rates (Qk, Qc, Qab, Qcm) and clinker production basis required to calculate PMalt per the equations in §63.1343(b)(2)? (collect design/operating flow data and clinker production rate)

Do you have, or will you install, a PM CPMS that provides 4–20 mA or digital output, with the required measurement range and annual performance test capability to establish a site-specific operating limit? (verify instrument make/model, range, output and QA/QC procedures per 40 CFR 63.1349(b)(1)(i) and 63.1350(b))

Are you able to perform Method 5 or 5I initial PM performance tests (three runs, minimum sample volumes, test conditions) and repeat annual tests as required? (verify test plan, lab, and sampling logistics per 40 CFR 63.1349(b)(1)(vi))

Do you continuously measure or have instruments to continuously measure and record stack gas flow rates (or available maximum design exhaust flow) to support mass-based lb/ton-clinker calculations? (verify flow monitoring per 40 CFR 63.1349(a) and 63.1350(n))

If considering reliance on other rules (e.g., NSPS for coal preparation plants), have you documented whether the coal mill is excluded from or covered by those rules and whether Subpart LLL explicitly covers this coal mill as an in-line coal mill? (compare applicability; Subpart LLL provisions cited in 40 CFR 63.1340(b)(1) and 63.1341)

Do records show whether previous performance tests measured PM (and whether coal mill and kiln were tested simultaneously) and do you have historical data to set/reassess the PM CPMS operating limit? (collect prior test reports and CPMS records)

judge_text: {"score":1,"reason":"The answer captures the Subpart LLL rationale (that an in‑line coal mill is treated as part of the kiln and PM must be combined/simultaneously tested and addressed with PM performance testing/CPMS per §§63.1343, 63.1349, 63.1350). It does not, however, identify or apply the EPA’s other key point that the coal mill is also subject to NSPS Subpart Y as a thermal dryer — the only mention of other rules is a generic checklist item and does not capture Subpart Y applicability. Therefore some but not all key EPA reasons are included."}

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Secondary Aluminum Production

criteria.criterion: If the facility meets the definition of a 'secondary aluminum production facility' in §63.1503, then the owner/operator is subject to Subpart RRR.

If the delamination/delacquering unit qualifies as a 'scrap dryer/delacquering kiln/decoating kiln' and it is located at a secondary aluminum production facility that is a major source of HAPs, then that unit is an affected source subject to the requirements of this subpart.

If the delamination/delacquering unit qualifies as a 'scrap dryer/delacquering kiln/decoating kiln' and it is located at a secondary aluminum production facility that is an area source of HAPs, then the dioxin/furan (D/F) requirements and associated operating/monitoring/reporting/recordkeeping provisions of this subpart apply to that unit.

If the facility is an aluminum die casting, aluminum foundry, or aluminum extrusion facility that only melts clean charge, customer returns, or internal scrap and does not operate sweat furnaces, thermal chip dryers, or scrap dryers/delacquering kilns/decoating kilns, then it is not considered a 'secondary aluminum production facility' for purposes of this subpart and Subpart RRR does not apply on that basis.

candidates.title: General Provisions

criteria.criterion: If an owner or operator is subject to Subpart RRR, then the general provisions in Subpart A identified as applicable in Appendix A to Subpart RRR apply to that owner or operator.

checklist: Do you meet the definition of a 'secondary aluminum production facility' in 40 CFR 63.1503 (i.e., do you use aluminum scrap or perform scrap shredding, scrap drying/delacquering/decoating, thermal chip drying, furnace operations, recovery of aluminum from dross, in-line fluxing, or dross cooling)?

Is the delamination chamber operated 'primarily to remove organic contaminants such as oil, paint, lacquer, ink, plastic, and/or rubber from aluminum scrap' (i.e., does it match the §63.1503 definition of a scrap dryer/delacquering kiln/decoating kiln)?

Is your facility a major source of HAPs (potential to emit ≥10 tons/year of any single listed HAP or ≥25 tons/year of combined HAPs)? (If unknown, calculate facility PTE to determine major vs. area source status.)

Is your facility an aluminum die casting, aluminum foundry, or aluminum extrusion facility that only melts clean charge, customer returns, or internal scrap AND does not operate sweat furnaces, thermal chip dryers, or scrap dryers/delacquering kilns/decoating kilns (per 40 CFR 63.1503 exemption)?

Do you perform any on-site melting, furnace operations, or other secondary-aluminum processes beyond delamination and grinding (e.g., shredding, thermal chip drying, dross recovery, furnaces, in-line fluxing)?

Is the delaminated/granulated product intended to be sold for remelting by you or your customers (i.e., is the unit used 'prior to melting' in the supply chain), or is it sold as a finished non-melted product?

For area-source consideration: if you are an area source, does the delamination unit nonetheless trigger the D/F-specific provisions (verify whether D/F requirements in 40 CFR 63.1500(c) and 63.1505(d)(1)(iii) apply)?

judge_text: {"score": 1, "reason": "The answer captures the main definitional basis (that the delamination chambers meet the §63.1503 definition of a scrap dryer/delacquering kiln/decoating kiln and thus can bring the source under Subpart RRR) but it fails to reflect the EPA's key point that, after the 2015 rule revisions, applicability no longer depends on whether the recovered aluminum is later melted. The checklist items and criteria implying dependence on subsequent melting/remelting contradict the EPA Notes and so the EPA's reasoning is only partially captured."}

candidates.title: Paint Stripping and Miscellaneous Surface Coating Operations (area source)

criteria.criterion: If you operate an area source of HAP and perform paint stripping using methylene chloride (MeCl) for removal of dried paint, then your paint stripping operation is subject to this subpart.

If you operate an area source of HAP and perform spray application of coatings to motor vehicles or mobile equipment, then your motor vehicle and mobile equipment surface coating operation is subject to this subpart.

If you operate an area source of HAP and perform spray application of coatings that contain target HAP (Cr, Pb, Mn, Ni, Cd at the concentrations specified in the definition) to plastic and/or metal substrates of parts or products (not motor vehicles or mobile equipment), then those surface coating operations are subject to this subpart.

If you are the owner/operator of a motor vehicle or mobile equipment surface coating operation and you can demonstrate that you spray apply no coatings that contain the target HAP, then you may petition the Administrator for an exemption from the surface coating provisions of this subpart or, on and after May 9, 2023, submit a notification to the Administrator in place of a petition (while retaining required records and allowing the Administrator to verify), and until circumstances change you need not be subject to the surface coating provisions.

If your surface coating or paint stripping activities fall within the exclusions (e.g., military installations/munitions, personal hobby maintenance under the thresholds, research and laboratory activities, quality control activities, or activities covered under another area source NESHAP), then those activities are not subject to this subpart.
If your source is not an area source (i.e., it is a major source as defined by emissions thresholds in §63.11170(b)), then the area-source standards of this subpart do not apply to you.

checklist: Confirm whether the facility is an area source (total HAP potential to emit < 10 tpy for any single HAP and < 25 tpy combined) per 40 CFR 63.11170(b).

Confirm whether you perform spray application of coatings to motor vehicles or mobile equipment at this location (fixed-location autobody/refinish) or only perform maintenance that meets the definition of facility maintenance in §63.11180.

Inventory every coating you spray-apply and verify, using manufacturer formulation data or MSDS, whether any coating contains any target HAP (chromium, lead, manganese, nickel, cadmium) at or above the rule thresholds (>=0.1% by mass for carcinogenic target HAP and >=1.0% by mass for other target HAP), evaluated on the coating as applied (per §63.11180).

If you spray-apply no target-HAP containing coatings, decide whether you will (a) petition the Administrator for an exemption or (b) submit the post-May 9, 2023 notification to the Administrator that you do not spray apply any target HAP containing coatings; prepare the descriptive documentation and certification of coatings used for that submission and retain on site.

If you use methylene chloride (MeCl) for paint stripping, record actual annual MeCl usage (tons/year); if >1 ton/year prepare and implement a written MeCl minimization plan, post the plan per §63.11173(b), and include MeCl usage reporting as required by §63.11176(b).

Maintain and retain required records: painter training certification and dates (§63.11177(a)), documentation of spray booth filter efficiency (§63.11177(b)), spray gun equivalency documentation if applicable (§63.11177(c)), copies of any notifications/reports submitted (§63.11177(d)), and records of MeCl usage and minimization plan if applicable (§63.11177(e)-(f)).
Verify whether any of the subpart's exclusions apply to your operations (military, hobby/private, research/lab, quality control, or covered under another area source NESHAP) per §63.11169(d).

If subject to the subpart and not relying on exemption, confirm compliance equipment and practices: certified painters, appropriate spray booths/preparation stations or mobile enclosures with required capture and filters, approved spray equipment/transfer efficiency, and compliant spray-gun cleaning practices per §63.11173(e)-(f).

Determine whether initial notification, notification of compliance status, and annual change reports must be submitted via CEDRI/CDX per the deadlines in §63.11175 and §63.11176, and gather the information required for those submissions.

judge_text: {"score":2,"reason":"All key EPA reasons are captured: the answer cites that MeCl paint stripping is subject (63.11170(a)(1)/63.11169(a)), that spray vehicle coating can be exempted if you certify/no target HAPs (63.11170(a)(2)/63.11175/63.11177), and it notes the obligation to submit notifications/comply if target HAPs are later used."}

candidates.title: Area Source Paint Stripping and Miscellaneous Surface Coating Operations (Subpart HHHHHH)

criteria.criterion: If you operate an area source of HAP and perform paint stripping using methylene chloride (MeCl), then the source is subject to this subpart.

If you operate an area source of HAP and perform spray application of coatings to motor vehicles or mobile equipment (except spray applications that meet the definition of facility maintenance), then the source is subject to this subpart.

If you operate an area source of HAP and perform spray application of coatings that contain the target HAP to a plastic and/or metal substrate on a part or product (except spray applications that meet the definition of facility maintenance or space vehicle), then the source is subject to this subpart.

If you are the owner or operator of a motor vehicle or mobile equipment surface coating operation and you demonstrate to the Administrator (or submit the post‑May 9, 2023 notification) that you spray apply no coatings that contain the target HAP, then you may be exempt from the surface coating provisions of this subpart.

If a spray-applied coating contains any individual target HAP at or above the specified thresholds (cadmium, chromium, lead, or nickel ≥ 0.1 percent by mass; manganese ≥ 1.0 percent by mass), then that coating meets the definition of a target HAP containing coating for this subpart.
If you are an area source and you do not perform any of the activities listed in 63.11170(a)(1)–(3), then you are not subject to this subpart for those activities.

candidates.title: Surface Coating of Miscellaneous Metal Parts and Products (Subpart MMMM)

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate a new, reconstructed, or existing affected source that uses 946 liters (250 gallons) per year or more of coatings that contain HAP in the surface coating of miscellaneous metal parts and products and the source is a major source (or is located at or part of a major source of HAP emissions), then the source is subject to this subpart.
If your coating operation uses only coatings, thinners, other additives, and cleaning materials that contain no organic HAP, then this subpart does not apply to that coating operation.

If your facility is an area source (i.e., not a major source and not located at or part of a major source of HAP), then the primary applicability condition in §63.3881(b) (which requires major source status in addition to the 250 gal/yr threshold) is not met.

If your surface coating operation falls within any of the exclusions listed in §63.3881(c)(2)–(17) (for example research/laboratory, facility maintenance, hobby, or other specific sectoral NESHAP coverage), then that operation is not subject to this subpart.

If your activity meets the definition of a coating operation and the affected-source boundaries in §63.3882 (coating operations, storage/mixing, conveying, and waste handling for the coating operation), then those emissions are the basis for determining applicability under this subpart.

checklist: Determine whether the facility is an area source or a major source of HAP (calculate potential to emit: ≥10 tons/year of any single HAP or ≥25 tons/year combined HAP makes it a major source).
Confirm whether the polyurea line uses spray application (hand‑held or automated atomizing device) as defined for spray-applied coating operations.
Verify the substrate and product type coated on the polyurea line (miscellaneous metal parts/products vs. assembled motor vehicles or mobile equipment).

Obtain and review manufacturer formulation data / MSDS for the polyurea coating(s) used on the line to confirm whether they contain any target HAP (Cr, Pb, Mn, Ni, Cd) and, if so, whether concentrations meet or exceed the thresholds (Cd, Cr, Pb, Ni ≥ 0.1% by mass; Mn ≥ 1.0% by mass).

If the polyurea line is part of a motor vehicle or mobile equipment surface coating operation, verify whether the owner/operator has submitted a petition or the post‑May 9, 2023 notification to the Administrator certifying that no target HAP-containing coatings are spray applied.

Determine annual usage (volume) of coatings that contain HAP at the facility (identify volumes per line and facility total) to evaluate the 946 L (250 gal)/yr threshold and to support any predominant-activity or facility-specific emission limit calculations.

Confirm whether any coatings, thinners, additives, or cleaning materials used anywhere in the facility contain organic HAP (if the facility truly uses only non‑HAP coatings/materials, Subpart MMMM may not apply per the exclusion).
Verify whether the polyurea spray activity could instead meet any exclusions (facility maintenance, research/laboratory, quality control, or other listed exclusions in §63.3881(c)).

judge_text: {"score":2,"reason":"The EPA Notes’ key points—that the area‑source surface coating NESHAP (Subpart HHHHHH) applies to spray operations only when the coatings contain target HAPs and that motor‑vehicle/mobile‑equipment coating is treated differently—are explicitly captured in OUR ANSWER (HHHHHH criteria discussing spray application of target‑HAP coatings, threshold definitions, the MV/ME provision/exemption, and checklist items to verify absence of target HAP)."}

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Stationary Combustion Turbines (Subpart YYYY)

criteria.criterion: if a stationary combustion turbine is an existing, new, or reconstructed stationary combustion turbine located at a major source of HAP, then this subpart applies to that affected source

if you commenced construction of the stationary combustion turbine after January 14, 2003, then the turbine is a new stationary combustion turbine and is subject to this subpart if located at a major source

if the stationary combustion turbine is a lean premix gas-fired stationary combustion turbine, then you must comply with the emission limitations and operating limitations in Table 1 and Table 2 of this subpart

if the stationary combustion turbine is a new or reconstructed lean premix gas-fired turbine, then compliance with this subpart is required upon startup if startup occurred after March 9, 2022 (or by March 9, 2022 if started on or before that date)

if the stationary combustion turbine is an emergency turbine or is located on the North Slope of Alaska, then it does not have to meet the requirements of this subpart except for initial notification requirements

if the stationary combustion turbine is existing (construction or reconstruction commenced on or before January 14, 2003) or has rated peak power output less than 1.0 MW, then it does not have to meet the requirements of this subpart (with stated exceptions)

if your stationary combustion turbine is not equipped with an oxidation catalyst and is required to comply with the formaldehyde emission limitation, then you must petition the Administrator for operating limitations that you will monitor to demonstrate compliance (or petition for approval of no additional operating limitations) and must not conduct the initial performance test until the petition is approved or disapproved

if you petition the Administrator for approval of additional operating limitations for a turbine without an oxidation catalyst, then your petition must identify the specific parameters to monitor, explain how those parameters affect HAP emissions, establish upper and/or lower parameter values, identify measurement and monitoring methods and instruments with their accuracy/precision, and identify recalibration frequency and methods

if you petition the Administrator for approval of no additional operating limitations for a turbine without an oxidation catalyst, then your petition must identify parameters that could change, discuss their relation to HAP emissions, explain why limits cannot be established, identify measurement/monitoring methods and recalibration, and explain why adopting limits is infeasible/unnecessary
if you are required to comply with the formaldehyde emission limitation and you use an oxidation catalyst, then you must continuously monitor your catalyst inlet temperature

if you are required to comply with the formaldehyde emission limitation and you are not using an oxidation catalyst, then you must continuously monitor any parameters specified in your approved petition to demonstrate compliance

if you are required to conduct performance tests for formaldehyde, then tests must be conducted at high load (100 percent ±10 percent), consist of three separate runs each at least one hour, and (after Sept 8, 2020) be under representative performance conditions excluding startup and shutdown and not during malfunctions

if you are required to comply with the formaldehyde emission limitation, then you must submit a Notification of Compliance Status including performance test results within the timeframes specified (including submission of performance test results before the close of business on the 60th calendar day following completion of the performance test)

if you must comply with emission and operating limitations, then you must operate and maintain the turbine, any air pollution control device, and monitoring equipment in a manner consistent with good air pollution control practices (and after Sept 8, 2020, at all times consistent with safety and good practices)

if you are subject to this subpart, then you must keep the records and reports required (including notifications, performance test records, monitoring records, deviation records, and the records required in Table 5) to show continuous compliance

if you are required to use a continuous monitoring system after September 8, 2020, then you must develop and implement a CMS quality control program with written procedures per § 63.8(d)(1) through (2) and retain those procedures for the life of the affected source or until no longer subject

checklist: Confirm whether the facility is a major source of HAP
Confirm the turbine construction/reconstruction start date (before or after January 14, 2003)
Confirm the turbine startup date relative to March 9, 2022
Confirm turbine type (is it a lean premix gas-fired stationary combustion turbine as defined by the subpart?)
Confirm whether the turbine is new, reconstructed, or existing per 63.6090 definitions
Confirm whether the turbine is an emergency unit or located on the North Slope of Alaska (exceptions)
Record the turbine rated peak power output to see if it is < 1.0 MW (exemption)
Confirm whether an oxidation catalyst is installed (you stated none) and document that status

If no catalyst, prepare a petition to the Administrator specifying the proposed monitored parameters (e.g., turbine speed and inlet air temperature) and include (per 63.6120(f)): identification of parameters, discussion of relationship to HAP emissions, proposed upper/lower limits, measurement/monitoring methods and instruments with accuracy/precision, and recalibration frequency/methods
If proposing no additional operating limitations, prepare a petition per 63.6120(g) addressing each required element explaining infeasibility
Do not perform the initial performance test for formaldehyde until the petition is approved or disapproved by the Administrator (if petitioning under 63.6120(e))

Prepare for performance testing at high load (100% ±10%), with three separate runs each lasting at least 1 hour, and document that test conditions are representative and exclude startup/shutdown and malfunctions
Plan to continuously monitor and log the parameters specified in any approved petition (and implement CMS QC program if a CMS is required after Sept 8, 2020)

Submit required notifications: Initial Notification per 63.6145 timelines, Notification of Intent to conduct initial performance test at least 60 days before the test, and Notification of Compliance Status including performance test results within regulatory timeframes (performance test results within 60 days per 63.6150(f))
Ensure ability to submit required performance test data electronically via EPA ERT/CEDRI or prepare alternate electronic file per 63.6150(f)

Establish recordkeeping and reporting practices to retain notifications, test reports, monitoring records, deviation logs, and Table 5 records for the required retention periods and to prepare semiannual compliance reports per 63.6150 and recordkeeping per 63.6155

judge_text: {"score":2,"reason":"The EPA Notes’ key points are reflected: the requirement to petition under 40 CFR 63.6120(e)–(f) for turbines without an oxidation catalyst is included, the need to identify/justify specific monitored parameters and limits (63.6120(f)) is captured (and the checklist even cites turbine speed and inlet air temperature), and the requirement to continuously monitor petition-specified parameters per 63.6125(b) is included. Therefore all key reasons in the Notes are present in the criteria."}

candidates.title: Metal Fabrication and Finishing Area Sources

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate an area source that is primarily engaged (≥50% of production over the prior continuous 12 months) in one of the nine metal fabrication and finishing source categories listed in §63.11514(a)(1)–(9), then the subpart applies to your facility.

If you perform dry abrasive blasting, machining, dry grinding/dry polishing with machines, spray painting, or welding operations that use materials that contain MFHAP or have the potential to emit MFHAP, then those affected sources are subject to this subpart.

If the activities at your site are limited to tool or equipment repair operations, facility maintenance, or quality control activities as defined in §63.11522, then those activities are not subject to this subpart.

If your welding affected source uses less than 2,000 pounds per year (rolling 12-month basis) of welding rod containing one or more MFHAP, then you are not required to comply with the Tier 1–3 requirements in §63.11516(f)(3)–(8) (though you must maintain welding-rod-usage records as required).

candidates.title: Shipbuilding and Ship Repair Operations

criteria.criterion: If your facility performs shipbuilding and ship repair operations and the facility is a major source of HAP, then the provisions of this subpart apply to the facility.

If you use a coating in volumes of less than 200 liters (52.8 gallons) per year and the total volume of coatings exempt under this provision does not exceed 1,000 liters (264 gallons) per year at the facility, then the provisions of this subpart do not apply to those low-usage coatings.

If coatings are applied with hand-held, nonrefillable aerosol containers or are unsaturated polyester resin (fiberglass lay-up) coatings, then the provisions of this subpart do not apply to those coatings.

candidates.title: Paint Stripping and Miscellaneous Surface Coating Operations at Area Sources

criteria.criterion: If you operate an area source of HAP (not a major source) and you perform one or more of the listed activities in §63.11170(a) (MeCl paint stripping; spray application of coatings to motor vehicles and mobile equipment; or spray application of coatings that contain the target HAP to plastic and/or metal substrates on a part or product), then you are subject to this subpart.

If you were not actively engaged in paint stripping and/or miscellaneous surface coating prior to September 17, 2007 and you commenced construction of new paint stripping or surface coating equipment after that date, then the affected source is a new source under this subpart.

If your spray coating applications meet the definition of facility maintenance in §63.11180 (i.e., they qualify as facility maintenance), then those spray coating applications are excluded from this subpart.

checklist: Determine whether the facility is an area source or a major source of HAP (calculate annual potential emissions and compare to 10 tons single HAP / 25 tons total HAP thresholds referenced in 40 CFR 63.11170(b)).

Establish whether the facility is 'primarily engaged' (≥50% of production over the prior continuous 12 months) in any of the nine metal fabrication & finishing source categories listed in 40 CFR 63.11514(a)(1)–(9); document production basis and calculation.

Inventory all activities: confirm whether you perform dry abrasive blasting, welding, spray painting, machining, or dry grinding/dry polishing with machines and whether those operations are part of commercial repair/production or are facility maintenance, tool/equipment repair, or quality control as defined in 40 CFR 63.11522.

For all coatings, solvents, and welding rods: collect MSDS/formulation data and verify MFHAP content against thresholds in 40 CFR 63.11522 (cadmium, chromium, lead, nickel ≥0.1% by weight; manganese ≥1.0% by weight) and determine whether paints contain 'target HAP' for Subpart HHHHHH.
Track annual usage (rolling 12-month) of welding rods containing MFHAP (lbs/year) to see if ≥2,000 lb/yr threshold is exceeded (triggers additional welding requirements) per 40 CFR 63.11516(f).

Track annual volumes per coating (liters or gallons/year) and total low-usage coating volumes to determine Subpart II low-usage exemption eligibility (per-coating <200 L/yr and total of such exempt coatings ≤1000 L/yr) per 40 CFR 63.781(b).
Determine whether spray coating is performed on motor vehicles/mobile equipment or on parts/products (affects applicability of Subpart HHHHHH §63.11170(a)(2)–(3)).

Determine whether any spray coating operations qualify as 'facility maintenance' (excluded activity) under the relevant definitions (check operational intent, frequency, and whether coatings are applied to items that routinely leave/return to facility).

For abrasive blasting: document whether blasting is performed in totally enclosed/unvented chambers, in vented enclosures (and whether capture is vented to a filtration control device), or on objects >8 ft in any dimension, as these affect management practices required by 40 CFR 63.11516(a).

For spray painting operations: document whether spray booths or spray rooms are used, whether booths have filters demonstrated to achieve ≥98% MFHAP capture (or waterwash equivalency), and whether spray guns are HVLP or equivalent and painters are trained and certified per 40 CFR 63.11516(d).
Document existing capture, control, and filtration devices and maintain manufacturer specifications and operation instructions on file as required (per 40 CFR 63.11516 and 63.11519).

Assemble records and dates for any painter training, filter efficiency demonstrations, equipment specs, welding emission observations, and the rolling 12-month usage logs (maintain on-site for required retention periods).

judge_text: {"score":1,"reason":"The EPA Notes’ primary reason—that ship building/repair is not one of the nine categories in 40 CFR 63.11514(a)—is reflected in YOUR ANSWER (requires ‘primarily engaged’ in one of the nine categories). However, the EPA also relied on the facility’s SIC/NAICS classification (and the EPA Q&A table) and the finding that the earlier fabricated structural-metal classification no longer describes the facility; YOUR ANSWER does not include an explicit check of SIC/NAICS classification or the EPA Q&A table. Therefore only some key reasons are captured."}

candidates.title: Area Source Standards for Metal Fabrication and Finishing Operations

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate an area source that is primarily engaged in operations in one of the nine metal fabrication and finishing source categories listed in § 63.11514(a)(1)–(9), then the source is subject to this subpart.

If you use materials that contain MFHAP or have the potential to emit MFHAP (per the MFHAP concentration thresholds), then the provisions of this subpart apply to the affected source(s) performing dry abrasive blasting, machining, dry grinding/polishing, spray painting, or welding that use or can emit MFHAP.

If the facility's production of one or more products listed in one of the nine source category descriptions in Table 1 represents at least 50 percent of the facility's production (using the appropriate metric) over the previous continuous 12 months, then the facility is 'primarily engaged' and the subpart's applicability test in § 63.11514(a) is met.
If an operation is tool or equipment repair, facility maintenance, or quality control as defined in § 63.11522, then that operation is not subject to this subpart.

If a given machining, dry grinding/dry polishing, dry abrasive blasting, spray painting, or welding operation does not use any materials containing MFHAP and does not have the potential to emit MFHAP, then the requirements for that specific operation in § 63.11516 (and related paragraphs) do not apply.

If your welding affected source uses 2,000 pounds or more per year of welding rod containing one or more MFHAP (rolling 12-month basis), then you must demonstrate implementation of management practices or fume control measures by complying with the Tier 1–Tier 3 and Site-Specific Welding Emissions Management Plan requirements in § 63.11516(f)(3)–(8).

candidates.title: Surface Coating of Miscellaneous Metal Parts and Products

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate an affected source that uses 946 liters (250 gallons) per year or more of coatings that contain HAP for surface coating of miscellaneous metal parts and products and the source is a major source (or located at / part of a major source of HAP), then the facility is subject to this subpart.

If your facility uses only coatings, thinners, additives, and cleaning materials that contain no organic HAP (as determined under § 63.3941(a)), then the surface coating operation is not subject to this subpart.

If coating types are used in volumes of less than 189 liters (50 gallons) per year and the total volume of coatings exempt under that provision does not exceed 946 liters (250 gallons) per year at the facility, then those coating activities may be exempt from this subpart.

If surface coating operations at the facility meet the applicability criteria of another final surface coating NESHAP listed in paragraph (e) and you elect to comply under that other NESHAP or determine a predominant activity/facility-specific limit per paragraph (e), then you may comply as allowed by § 63.3881(e) instead of complying solely under this subpart.

checklist: Confirm whether the facility is an 'area source' (not a major source) of HAP and document the basis for that determination.
Identify which of the nine metal fabrication and finishing source categories (see Table 1 of Subpart XXXXXX) best describes your primary product(s) and obtain Table 1 to verify category descriptions.

Calculate the fraction of facility production represented by manufacturing/fabricating the product(s) listed in the applicable category over the previous continuous 12 months (use appropriate metric: volume, linear foot, square foot, or other industry-suitable metric) to determine if ≥50% (the 'primarily engaged' test).

Determine whether your facility activity is true manufacturing/fabrication of those products versus assembly/repair from purchased components (document how products are produced and whether manufacturing/fabrication is performed on-site).

Collect Material Safety Data Sheets (MSDS) / formulation data for all paints, coatings, welding rods, abrasives, base metals, and other consumables to determine MFHAP content (cadmium, chromium, lead, nickel ≥ 0.1% by weight; manganese ≥ 1.0% by weight) and whether materials 'contain MFHAP'.

Inventory annual usage (rolling 12-month) of coatings (in liters or gallons of product and liters/gallons of solids if needed) and determine how many liters per year of coatings containing HAP are used to evaluate the 946 L/yr (250 gal/yr) threshold in Subpart MMMM.

Inventory annual welding rod usage (rolling 12-month) and determine whether welding rods containing MFHAP total ≥2,000 lb/yr to trigger additional welding control/monitoring requirements under § 63.11516(f).

Document which finishing processes are 'dry' (dry machining, dry grinding, dry abrasive blasting) and whether they use or have the potential to emit MFHAP; verify if abrasive blasting is 'totally enclosed and unvented' or 'vented' and size of items blasted (>8 ft dimension) for applicable management practices.

Determine whether spray painting at the facility is 'spray-applied painting' as defined (atomized methods) and identify whether spray booths/rooms or other application/controls are used; document whether fewer than half of products receive finishing steps (note: do not assume this alone determines 'primarily engaged').

Verify whether any operations are properly characterized as tool/equipment repair, facility maintenance, or quality control per the definitions in § 63.11522, since those activities are exempt from Subpart XXXXXX.

If evaluating Subpart MMMM applicability, determine whether the facility is a 'major source' of HAP (emit or have potential to emit ≥10 t/yr single HAP or ≥25 t/yr combined HAP) or is located at/part of a major source.

Retain documentation used for all applicability determinations (production metrics, MSDS/formulation data, usage records, maintenance/repair definitions) for at least 5 years as required by § 63.11519(c)(1)(ii).

These capture the key points in the EPA notes (category assignment and how 'primarily engaged' is judged)." }

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants for Stationary Reciprocating Internal Combustion Engines (RICE)

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate a stationary RICE located at a major or area source of HAP emissions (and it is not a stationary RICE test cell/stand), then the engine is subject to Subpart ZZZZ.

If the engine is a non-road engine (as defined in 40 CFR 1068.30) or is used to propel a motor vehicle or a vehicle used solely for competition, then it is not a stationary RICE and is not subject to Subpart ZZZZ.
If the engine is being tested at a stationary RICE test cell/stand, then it is not subject to Subpart ZZZZ.

If the engine meets the definition of an emergency stationary RICE in §63.6675 and operates according to the provisions in §63.6640(f), then the emergency stationary RICE listed in §63.6585(f) are not subject to this subpart.

If your engine meets any of the criteria in §63.6590(c) such that it must meet the requirements of 40 CFR part 60 (subpart IIII for compression ignition or JJJJ for spark ignition), then it must meet part 60 and no further requirements apply under this part.

If your plant is a major source of HAPs (any single HAP ≥10 tons/year or any combination ≥25 tons/year), then RICE at that plant are being evaluated as located at a major source for applicability under this subpart.

If the stationary RICE meets the limited-exception conditions in §63.6590(b)(1) (for example a new or reconstructed emergency or limited-use RICE >500 HP at a major source), then the RICE does not have to meet the requirements of this subpart except for the initial notification requirements of §63.6645(f).

checklist: For each diesel engine, record whether it is a non-road engine or is used to propel a vehicle (i.e., does it propel the vacuum unit or only power the vacuum pump and accessories).
For each engine, record the manufacturer's site-rated brake horsepower (HP).
For each engine, record the fuel type (confirm compression-ignition diesel).
For each engine, record the date you commenced construction or reconstruction (to determine new vs existing under §63.6590).

For each engine, record annual hours of operation and whether operation is only during emergencies or includes routine/maintenance/non-emergency use (to determine emergency or limited-use status and potential <100-hr limited use).
Determine whether the engine is ever operated at a stationary RICE test cell/stand.
Estimate actual and potential-to-emit annual HAP emissions for the facility (tons/year for single HAP and combined HAP) to determine area vs major source status (≥10 tpy single or ≥25 tpy combined).
Determine whether the engine is subject to 40 CFR part 60 NSPS (e.g., subpart IIII for CI engines) (new/reconstructed status, date, and other part 60 applicability criteria).

If claiming 'emergency stationary RICE' status, document how the engine meets the emergency definition in §63.6675 and the operating limits in §63.6640(f) (frequency, purpose, any financial arrangements).
Document whether any fuel combusted is landfill or digester gas (relevant to certain exceptions in §63.6590).
