It also does not explicitly tie the applicability to §63.6675’s location/residency rule. Thus only some key reasons are present."}

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Engine Test Cells/Stands (Engine Test Cell/Stand NESHAP)

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate an engine test cell/stand that is located at a major source of HAP emissions, then the source is subject to this subpart.

If the apparatus is used for testing uninstalled stationary or uninstalled mobile (motive) engines, then it is an engine test cell/stand for purposes of this subpart (and if it is not testing uninstalled engines then it is not an engine test cell/stand under this subpart).

If the engine test cells/stands are located at a plant site that emits or has the potential to emit any single HAP at a rate of 10 tons per year or more or any combination of HAP at 25 tons per year or more, then the subpart applies (major source threshold).

If the affected source is an existing affected source that commenced construction or reconstruction on or before May 14, 2002, then the existing affected source does not have to meet the requirements of this subpart and of subpart A of this part.

If any portion of a new or reconstructed affected source located at a major source is used exclusively for testing internal combustion engines with rated power of less than 25 horsepower, then that portion does not have to meet the requirements of this subpart and of subpart A except for the initial notification requirement in § 63.9345(b).

If any portion of a new or reconstructed affected source located at a major source is used exclusively for testing combustion turbine engines, rocket engines, research and teaching activities at non‑commercial facilities, or testing/evaluating fuels, transmissions, or electronics, then that portion does not have to meet the requirements of this subpart and of subpart A.

If you operate a new or reconstructed affected source that is used in whole or in part for testing internal combustion engines with rated power of 25 hp or more and that is located at a major source, then you must comply with the emission limitations in Table 1 to this subpart.

If you use add‑on control devices on a new or reconstructed affected source, then you must meet the operating limits specified in Table 2 to this subpart (established during the performance test) and, if you install CEMS, must install, operate, and maintain them as required in this subpart.

checklist: Confirm whether each tested engine is 'uninstalled' (not installed in or an integrated part of the final product).
Confirm that the testing apparatus is an engine test cell/stand used for testing uninstalled stationary or uninstalled mobile engines.
Determine whether the plant/site is a major source of HAPs (any single HAP ≥10 tpy or total HAPs ≥25 tpy) based on potential to emit.
Determine whether the affected source is existing (construction/reconstruction commenced on or before May 14, 2002) or new/reconstructed (commenced after May 14, 2002).
For new/reconstructed portions, determine whether any portion is used exclusively for testing internal combustion engines <25 hp (19 kW).

For new/reconstructed portions, determine whether any portion is exclusively for combustion turbine engines, rocket engines, non‑commercial research/teaching, or for testing/evaluating fuels, transmissions, or electronics.
Document the rated power of the engines tested (hp) to check the 25 hp applicability threshold.

Verify whether add‑on control devices or CEMS are installed or planned (which would trigger the operating limits, CEMS installation, performance evaluation, and ongoing monitoring/maintenance requirements).
If subject, verify applicable compliance deadlines and performance test requirements (e.g., initial compliance demonstrations, performance evaluations, and CEMS performance specifications).

These missing elements are key reasons in the EPA notes."}

candidates.title: Coal- and Oil-Fired Electric Utility Steam Generating Units (Utility MACT / Mercury and Air Toxics Rule)

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate a coal-fired EGU or an oil-fired EGU as defined in § 63.10042, then your unit is subject to this subpart.
If your unit is an electric utility steam generating unit that is not a coal- or oil-fired EGU and that meets the definition of a natural gas-fired EGU, then it is not subject to this subpart.

If your unit has the capability of combusting more than 25 MW of coal or oil but did not fire sufficient coal or oil to satisfy the average annual heat input thresholds for coal- or oil-fired EGUs in § 63.10042, then it is not subject to this subpart under that capability-based exclusion.

candidates.title: Major Source Industrial, Commercial, and Institutional Boilers and Process Heaters (Major-Source Boiler MACT)

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate an industrial, commercial, or institutional boiler or process heater located at or part of a major source of HAP as defined in this subpart, then your unit is subject to this subpart unless excluded by § 63.7491.

If the boiler is an electric utility steam generating unit (EGU) covered by subpart UUUUU or a natural gas-fired EGU firing at least 85 percent natural gas on an annual heat input basis, then it is not subject to this subpart.

checklist: Confirm the unit's gross electric output (is it >25 MWe?) and whether it serves a generator that produces electricity for sale (check EGU status per 40 CFR 63.10042).
Verify which fuels are allowed by the unit's permit and whether the site has the necessary fuel handling capability for coal or oil (to determine 'fossil fuel-fired' capability per 40 CFR 63.10042).

Calculate the unit's fuel heat-input fractions: percent oil, percent coal, and percent natural gas based on heat input for the previous 3 calendar years (three-year average) and for each single year (to compare to the >10% average / >15% single-year thresholds in § 63.10042).

Determine whether oil usage (including startup oil firing) is under 10% of average annual heat input over the last 3 years and under 15% in any single year (these thresholds determine 'oil-fired EGU' status under 40 CFR 63.10042).
If the unit is primarily natural gas, calculate whether it burns at least 85% natural gas on an annual heat input basis (relevant to the exclusion in 40 CFR 63.7491(a)).
Determine whether the facility is a 'major source of HAP' (PTE criteria per the major source definition in 40 CFR part 63/§ 63.2 or § 63.7575 as applicable).

If applicable, verify whether the unit changed fuel usage or operation after the compliance date and whether the 6‑month continued-subject provisions or conversion provisions in § 63.10000 apply (e.g., permanent conversion to natural gas/biomass).

Collect fuel usage records and heat-input calculations (boiler operating day and annual heat input data) needed to demonstrate applicability under the three-year rolling evaluation described in 40 CFR 63.10042 and related sections.

judge_text: {"score":2,"reason":"EPA’s key points — oil <10% (3‑yr avg) and <15% (single year) means not an oil‑fired EGU under §63.10042 (so UUUUU doesn’t apply), and as a natural‑gas‑fired EGU it is excluded from DDDDD under §63.7491(a) — are all reflected in the provided criteria and checklist (§63.10042 oil thresholds, UUUUU natural‑gas exclusion, and DDDDD §63.7491(a)/85% natural gas exclusion)."}

candidates.title: Pesticide Active Ingredient Production (Subpart MMM)

criteria.criterion: If the facility-wide collection of pesticide active ingredient manufacturing process units (PAI process units) that process, use, or produce HAP are located at a plant site that is a major source, then the facility is an affected source subject to this subpart.
If the process is a research and development facility, then the provisions of this subpart do not apply to that facility.
If a PAI process unit is subject to subpart F of this part, then that PAI process unit is excluded from the requirements of this subpart MMM.

If a storage vessel's input from the PAI process unit is greater than or equal to the input from any other process unit, or its output to the PAI process unit is greater than or equal to the output to any other process unit, then that storage vessel is part of the affected PAI process unit (and hence falls under this subpart for applicability purposes).

If construction or reconstruction of an affected source commenced after November 10, 1997, or a dedicated PAI process unit commenced construction after November 10, 1997 and has the potential to emit >= 10 tons/yr of any one HAP or >= 25 tons/yr combined HAP, then the source or dedicated unit is a new affected source subject to the new-source provisions of this subpart.

candidates.title: Miscellaneous Organic Chemical Manufacturing (Subpart FFFF)

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate miscellaneous organic chemical manufacturing process units (MCPU) that are located at, or are part of, a plant site that is a major source of HAP, then those MCPUs are subject to this subpart.

If the equipment produces materials described by the referenced SIC/NAICS classifications, and the MCPU processes, uses, or generates any of the organic HAP listed in section 112(b), then the equipment meets the MCPU definition and is subject to this subpart, unless excluded by the listed exemptions.

If the MCPU is an affected source or part of an affected source under another subpart of part 63, then the MCPU is not subject to this subpart FFFF (except for the batch process vent exception noted in the rule).

If the distillation unit is a nondedicated solvent recovery operation (i.e., a distillation unit or other purification equipment that receives used solvent from more than one MCPU), then it is addressed as a nondedicated solvent recovery operation under the definitions and treatment of this subpart.
citations: 40 CFR 63.2550 (definition of nondedicated solvent recovery operation)

candidates.title: Chemical Manufacturing Process Units (Subpart F)

criteria.criterion: If a chemical manufacturing process unit (CMPU) manufactures as a primary product one or more chemicals listed in the subpart or uses/manufactures organic HAP listed in table 2 and is located at a plant site that is a major source, then the provisions of subparts F, G, and H apply to that CMPU.

If a distillation unit is dedicated to a chemical manufacturing process unit that is subject to this subpart, then each vent from that distillation unit is part of the source to which subpart F applies (i.e., the distillation vents must be evaluated under subpart F applicability).

If a distillation unit is not dedicated and the greatest input to the distillation unit is from a CMPU located on the same plant site (or the greatest input comes from an off-site CMPU but the greatest recipient on-site receives the most from the unit), then the distillation unit shall be assigned to that CMPU for applicability determinations under this subpart.

checklist: Confirm whether your Michigan site is a 'major source' under CAA section 112 (calculate annual HAP emissions by species to determine >=10 tpy single or >=25 tpy combined).

Confirm whether the material you produce (2,4‑D active ingredient) is a pesticide active ingredient (PAI) as defined (FIFRA/63.1361) and whether the herbicide manufacturing equipment is a PAI process unit.
Determine whether the new distillation column will be dedicated to the PAI process (serves only the herbicide/PAI process) or will be shared (receive or send material to multiple processes).

For storage tanks in the neighboring building that hold the purchased raw material, determine the greatest input to and/or output from each tank (which process supplies or receives the most) to decide assignment to the PAI process unit per 40 CFR 63.1360(f).
Determine whether any storage vessel was already subject to another Part 63 subpart on June 23, 1999 (which would assign it to that other subpart per 63.1360(f)(1)).

Estimate the potential-to-emit (tons/yr) of HAP from the new distillation/process (before controls) to see if the 10 tpy / 25 tpy thresholds for 'new dedicated PAI' or MCPU dedicated-unit treatment are met.

Document the construction/reconstruction commencement date for the distillation column and compare to the new-source cutoffs referenced in the subparts (e.g., Subpart MMM Nov 10, 1997; Subpart FFFF Apr 4, 2002; and the dates in 40 CFR 63.100 for CMPU/new-source determinations).
Verify whether the distillation is a nondedicated solvent recovery operation (does it receive used solvent from more than one MCPU?), per the definition in 40 CFR 63.2550.
Confirm whether the operation could qualify as research & development or another exemption listed in the subparts (e.g., MMM(d)(1), FFFF(c) exemptions).

Check whether the PAI process unit (or distillation) is already being regulated under another Part 63 subpart (e.g., subpart F/CMPU) because that may change which subpart applies (see 40 CFR 63.1360(d)(2) and 40 CFR 63.2435(b)(3)).

judge_text: {"score":1,"reason":"Some key reasons are captured (the answer lists MMM and FFFF as candidates and includes checklist items to confirm the unit is a pesticide active‑ingredient PAI process and whether the distillation is dedicated or shared), but it fails to explicitly capture the EPA’s core rationale that HON (subparts F/G) would not apply because the distillation serves a pesticide (PAI) process rather than a SOCMI unit. The answer even includes Subpart F applicability criteria without clarifying the SOCMI exclusion that EPA relied on."}

candidates.title: Definitions for chemical preparations area source

criteria.criterion: If the cathode slurry mixing is a chemical preparation operation (mixing, blending, milling, or extruding) performed under NAICS code 325998 and the materials processed are target HAP-containing (e.g., nickel at ≥0.1 percent by weight as metal), then the operation is subject to this subpart.

candidates.title: Paints and allied products manufacturing area source

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate a paints and allied products manufacturing facility that is an area source and the facility processes, uses, or generates materials containing HAP (including dry pigments or solids that contain nickel), then the paints and allied products area source standards apply to the affected source.

If during addition of dry pigments or solids that contain nickel you do not capture particulate emissions and route them to a particulate control device as required, then you are not meeting the requirements of this subpart.

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants for Surface Coating of Miscellaneous Metal Parts and Products (area source)

criteria.criterion: If the cathode process includes surface coating of metal parts or products (for example, coating metal foil) then the affected source includes all coating operations and the storage containers and mixing vessels in which coatings and additives are stored or mixed, and thus may be subject to this subpart.

checklist: Determine the facility NAICS code for the cathode slurry/mixing operation (is it NAICS 325998?).
Confirm whether the cathode mixing is performed as a chemical preparation operation (mixing/blending/milling/extruding) versus a surface coating or paint-manufacturing activity.
Obtain formulation/SDS data for the active material, binder, and solvent to verify nickel content in the materials as used (is nickel ≥ 0.1% by weight as metal?).
Determine whether the operation is located at an area source (potential to emit each HAP < 10 tpy and total HAPs < 25 tpy).

Determine if the slurry mixing and subsequent coating constitute a surface coating operation on metal foil (coating of a metal substrate) and whether coating/mixing vessels store or mix coatings/additives.

If treating the material as a paint/allied product process, document whether dry pigments/solids containing nickel are added in dry form or only as paste/slurry/liquid and whether capture and particulate control are provided during additions.

Check whether any Table 1 CMPU HAPs (e.g., manganese, quinoline, trivalent chromium, hydrazine, or other Table 1 HAPs) are present above the concentrations specified in 40 CFR 63.11494(a)(2) to evaluate applicability of the CMPU rule.
Document whether the operation is primarily engaged in any of the nine source categories listed in Subpart XXXXXX (metal fabrication/finishing) to assess that subpart's potential applicability.

judge_text: {"score":2,"reason":"OUR ANSWER includes the paint/allied-products subpart (CCCCCCC), checks for nickel as a HAP (verify ≥0.1%/SDS), and asks to determine whether the slurry/coating leaves a dried film or is a surface-coating vs a chemical-preparation (NAICS 325998) — thus capturing the EPA notes that the line is a paint/coating (not chemical manufacturing) because it leaves a dried film and contains nickel."}

candidates.title: Glass Manufacturing Area Source Standards

criteria.criterion: if you own or operate a glass manufacturing facility that is an area source and the facility uses one or more continuous furnaces charged with compounds of one or more glass manufacturing metal HAP as raw materials in a glass manufacturing batch formulation, then the facility is subject to this subpart

if a glass melting furnace is a continuous furnace, is charged with compounds of one or more glass manufacturing metal HAP as raw materials, and is used to produce glass that contains one or more glass manufacturing metal HAP at a rate of at least 45 Mg/yr (50 tpy), then that furnace is an affected furnace under this subpart
if a furnace is a research and development process unit as defined in the subpart, then that furnace is not an affected furnace under this subpart

candidates.title: Paints and Allied Products Area Source Standards

criteria.criterion: if you own or operate a facility that performs paints and allied products manufacturing that is an area source and the facility processes, uses, or generates materials containing HAP then the facility (the affected source consisting of all paints and allied products manufacturing processes that process, use, or generate materials containing HAP) is subject to this subpart

if the material you manufacture is a paints and allied product (a material intended to be applied to a substrate and leave a dried film of solid material; typically described by NAICS 3255 and 3259 and produced by physical means such as blending and mixing), then the paints and allied products manufacturing definitions and standards in this subpart apply
if a facility no longer processes, uses, or generates materials containing HAP and does not plan to do so in the future, then the affected source is no longer subject to this subpart
if the facility is a research and development facility as defined in CAA section 112(c)(7), then it is not subject to this subpart

candidates.title: Chemical Preparations Area Source Standards

criteria.criterion: if you own or operate a chemical preparations facility that is a stationary area source of HAP and the facility has at least one chemical preparations operation in target HAP service, then the facility is subject to this subpart and the affected source consists of all chemical preparations operations at the facility

if the operation is a chemical preparations operation described by NAICS code 325998 (mixing, blending, milling, extruding equipment used to manufacture chemical preparations), then it meets the subpart's definition of chemical preparation/operation

if the chemical preparations operations at your facility are subject to subpart VVVVVV (chemical manufacturing area source) or subpart CCCCCCC (paints and allied products), then this subpart's requirements do not apply to those operations
if the operations are research and development facilities as defined in section 112(c)(7) of the CAA, then they are not subject to this subpart

candidates.title: Chemical Manufacturing Area Source Standards (CMPU)

criteria.criterion: if you own or operate a chemical manufacturing process unit (CMPU) located at an area source and Table 1 HAP are present in the CMPU according to the specified thresholds (e.g., the CMPU uses as feedstock any material that contains quinoline, manganese, and/or trivalent chromium at >1.0 percent by weight, or any other Table 1 HAP at >0.1 percent by weight), then the CMPU is subject to this subpart

if a CMPU includes process vessels, equipment, and activities necessary to operate a chemical manufacturing process that produces a material described by NAICS code 325 (i.e., CMPU defined as NAICS 325 production), then that unit is within the scope of the subpart
if the operations fall into the listed exclusions (for example, manufacture of Paint and Allied Products that are subject to subpart CCCCCCC), then this subpart does not apply to those operations

if a CMPU is located at an area source that installed a federally-enforceable control device necessary to maintain the source's emissions at area source levels, then the facility may be required to obtain a permit under 40 CFR part 70 or 71 as specified in this subpart

checklist: Determine the primary NAICS code(s) for the frit/glass operation (confirm whether the operation is reported as NAICS 3255, NAICS 325998, or another NAICS 325 code).
Determine whether the facility is an area source (calculate potential-to-emit for individual HAP and total HAP and compare to 10 tpy single HAP and 25 tpy combined HAP thresholds).

Confirm whether the frit is produced by melting raw materials into molten glass and quenching (i.e., whether the operation meets the "glass manufacturing facility" description and whether product is produced by melting/forming molten glass).

For each melting furnace, verify whether it is a continuous furnace as defined in the applicable subpart and whether it is charged with compounds of metal HAP (check feedstock/SDS for metal HAP compounds such as nickel).
For each furnace, record the annual production rate of glass produced from that furnace (Mg/yr or tpy) to determine if it meets or exceeds 45 Mg/yr (50 tpy) per 40 CFR 63.11449(a)(3).

Check whether the raw materials, feedstocks, intermediates, or products contain target metal HAP (nickel, chromium, manganese, lead, cadmium) and quantify concentrations from formulation data or SDS (compare to thresholds used by VVVVVV and BBBBBBB, e.g., >1.0% or >0.1% as applicable).

Determine whether the frit product or processes are paints and allied products (i.e., materials intended to be applied to a substrate and leave a dried film) or whether the frit is an ingredient used in coatings but not itself a paint product; confirm intended use and manufacturing steps (blending/mixing vs. melting glass).
Determine whether the frit production includes chemical preparations operations (mixing, blending, milling, extruding) that would fall under NAICS 325998 chemical preparations operation definitions.

Determine whether any portion of the operation qualifies as a chemical manufacturing process unit (CMPU) under NAICS 325 and whether Table 1 HAP (see subpart VVVVVV Table 1) are present in feedstocks, byproducts, or products at the concentration thresholds in 40 CFR 63.11494(a)(2).
Confirm whether any units or operations are research and development process units (R&D) that would be excluded from affected-source status under the applicable subparts.

If the facility handles dry pigments or solids containing metal HAP (cadmium, chromium, lead, nickel) and performs additions or grinding/milling, document whether capture systems and particulate control devices are used per the paints rule requirements.
Determine whether any chemical preparations operations are already subject to subpart VVVVVV or subpart CCCCCCC (if so, those operations are exempt from subpart BBBBBBB per 40 CFR 63.11579(f)).

Check whether any federally-enforceable control device was installed to keep the source at area-source emissions levels (if yes, determine whether a title V permit is required per 40 CFR 63.11494(e)).

judge_text: {"score":2,"reason":"All key EPA reasons are reflected: the paints subpart criteria include the NAICS 3255/’leaves a dried film’ definition; the checklist and VVVVVV criteria reference the relevant HAP concentration thresholds (including the >0.1% convention noted) to identify HAP-containing material; BBBBBBB is limited to NAICS 325998 and that distinction is captured; and VVVVVV’s exclusion for sources subject to the paints subpart (63.11494(c)(1)(i)) is included. Thus the EPA Notes’ principal points are present in the criteria."}

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Secondary Aluminum Production

criteria.criterion: if the facility is a secondary aluminum production facility as defined in 40 CFR 63.1503, then the requirements of this subpart apply to the owner or operator of the facility (i.e., the subpart is potentially applicable to units at the facility).

if the facility is a secondary aluminum production facility that is a major source of hazardous air pollutants (HAPs), then each thermal chip dryer at the facility is an affected source subject to the emission standards and requirements in this subpart.

if the facility is a secondary aluminum production facility that is an area source of HAPs, then the dioxin/furan (D/F) requirements of this subpart apply to each thermal chip dryer at the facility (even where other major-source requirements do not apply).

if the unit is used solely to remove water from aluminum scrap (for example a pre-heating box or dryer used only to remove water), then it is not considered a thermal chip dryer for purposes of this subpart and the thermal chip dryer listings/requirements do not apply.

if the unit is used primarily to remove paint, lacquer, ink, plastic, and/or rubber from aluminum scrap, then it is classified as a scrap dryer/delacquering kiln/decoating kiln (not a thermal chip dryer) and is subject to the scrap dryer/delacquering kiln/decoating kiln provisions and limits in this subpart.

if the unit processes painted or coated/shredded scrap (i.e., is not limited to unpainted/uncoated chips), then it does not meet the subpart's definition of a thermal chip dryer (which is for unpainted/uncoated chips) and should be evaluated as a scrap dryer/delacquering/decoating unit or other affected source under this subpart.

checklist: Determine whether your facility meets the definition of a "secondary aluminum production facility" in 40 CFR 63.1503 (list of processes performed on-site).
Determine whether the facility is a major source or an area source of HAPs (potential to emit considering controls: ≥10 tpy single HAP or ≥25 tpy combined HAPs).

Document the exact purpose of the new dryer: (a) is it intended to evaporate oil/water from unpainted/uncoated aluminum chips, (b) to remove water only, or (c) to remove paint/coatings/organic contaminants from shredded scrap?
Confirm the physical characteristics of the feedstock the dryer will process: painted/coated shredded aluminum vs unpainted/uncoated chips (size, origin, typical contaminant types and loads).
If the unit will process painted or coated scrap, verify whether it should be classified and permitted as a scrap dryer/delacquering/decoating kiln rather than a thermal chip dryer.

If claiming the unit is only a water-removal/pre-heat dryer, document operating mode and process descriptions showing no oil/paint removal to support that it is not a "thermal chip dryer" per the definition.

Identify planned control devices (afterburner, fabric filter, lime injection, etc.) and planned operating practices (e.g., will the thermal dryer be operated only on unpainted chips as required for thermal chip dryers under §63.1506(f)(3)?).

Record planned operating temperatures and residence times (for control design), but note applicability is determined by unit function/definition and facility/source status, not by a specific temperature threshold for D/F formation in the rule text.

If the facility is an aluminum die casting, foundry, or extrusion facility, verify whether the facility meets the limited conditions in §63.1500(f) that affect whether it is treated as a secondary aluminum production facility under this subpart.

judge_text: {"score": 2, "reason": "EPA's notes hinge on (1) the unit is a scrap dryer/delacquering kiln when drying painted scrap per 63.1503, and (2) the applicant cannot avoid applicability by citing a 660°F temperature without demonstrating no HAP emissions (i.e., applicability is based on function/feedstock, not a temperature threshold), and thus must meet major-source requirements. The submitted criteria explicitly include classification of painted-scrap units as scrap dryers, the need to evaluate painted vs unpainted feedstock, and a checklist note that applicability is determined by unit function/definition (not temperature) and to determine major vs area source—so the EPA key reasons are captured."}
