candidates.title: National emission standards for hazardous air pollutants for rubber tire manufacturing

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate a rubber tire manufacturing facility that is located at, or is a part of, a major source of hazardous air pollutant (HAP) emissions, then you are subject to this subpart.

If your facility is engaged in the manufacture of rubber tires or their components (including production of rubber tires and/or components integral to rubber tires, tire cord production, or application of puncture sealant), then this subpart applies to affected sources at your facility.

If the affected source at your facility includes tire production processes that use or process cements and solvents (for example, tread and cement operations, tire repair operations, green tire spray, slab dip, etc.), then those processes constitute the tire production affected source subject to the emission limits and requirements of this subpart.

If the stationary source (or group of stationary sources within a contiguous area under common control) emits or has the potential to emit any single HAP at a rate of 9.07 megagrams (10 tons) or more per year, or any combination of HAP at a rate of 22.68 megagrams (25 tons) or more per year, then it is a major source and the facility is subject under § 63.5981.

If your affected source is a tire cord production affected source but the primary product produced at that affected source is determined to be subject to another subpart as of that subpart's effective date or startup, then the rubber tire manufacturing subpart does not apply to that affected source (you must determine which subpart applies).

If your rubber tire manufacturing affected source is a research and development facility whose primary purpose is R&D into new processes/products, operated under close supervision of technically trained personnel and not engaged in manufacture of products for commercial sale except de minimis, then this subpart does not apply to that affected source.

If you do not own or operate a rubber tire manufacturing facility that is located at, or is part of, a major source of HAP emissions (i.e., your facility is not a major source as defined in § 63.5981), then you are not subject to this subpart.

checklist: Determine whether your facility performs 'manufacture of rubber tires or their components' (does it manufacture new tires or components, or only perform retreading/repair?).

Inventory all processes at the facility and confirm whether retread/repair operations use or process cements and solvents (identify specific operations: tread/cement operations, undertread, bead cementing, green tire spray, slab dip, marking, cleaning, etc.).
Prepare an inventory of all cements and solvents used (as purchased), including MSDS/CPDS or HAP mass percent for each material.

Calculate the facility's potential to emit (PTE) HAPs (single HAP and combined) accounting for all stationary sources under common control within the contiguous area to determine whether the facility is a major source (>= 10 tpy single HAP or >= 25 tpy combined HAP).
Determine whether your facility is part of a larger stationary source under common control and within a contiguous area (to decide whether emissions aggregate for major source determination).
If you have tire cord production, determine the primary product produced at the affected source over the relevant 5-year period and whether that primary product is subject to another NESHAP subpart.

Confirm whether the affected source is a research and development facility as defined (primary purpose R&D, close supervision by technically trained personnel, not engaged in commercial manufacture except de minimis).

If subject, identify whether tire production affected source processes are routed to controls or whether you will comply via purchase limits (collect data on rubber used per month, mass of cements/solvents used monthly, and any control device efficiencies) — this information will be needed for compliance demonstrations if the subpart applies.

judge_text: {"score":2,"reason":"EPA's sole key reason — the facilities are not major sources of HAP and therefore the NESHAP does not apply — is directly reflected in the answer: the criteria include the major source thresholds (10 tpy single / 25 tpy combined per 40 CFR 63.5981) and explicitly state that non‑major sources are not subject; checklist also requires PTE and aggregation determinations."}

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Petroleum Refinery Catalytic Cracking and Catalytic Reforming Units (Subpart UUU)

criteria.criterion: if the process vent is the catalytic cracking unit catalyst regenerator vent at a petroleum refinery then the source is within the scope of this subpart

if the catalytic cracking unit regenerator does not introduce any other gas streams into the catalyst regeneration vent (i.e., is a complete combustion unit with no additional combustion devices) then you may use the alternative air-flow-and-temperature-based procedure in § 63.1573(a)(1) instead of a continuous parameter monitoring system to determine the catalytic regenerator exhaust gas flow rate

if you have a gas analyzer installed in the catalytic cracking regenerator exhaust vent prior to the addition of air or other gas streams (measuring CO2, CO, and O2, and measured upstream of any CO boiler) then you may use the alternative calculation procedure in § 63.1573(a)(2) to calculate Qr, the volumetric flow rate of exhaust gas from the catalyst regenerator

if you elect Option 1b (NSPS PM coke burn-off) or Option 2 (PM per coke burn-off) under § 63.1564(a)(1)(ii) or (iv) then you must compute the PM emission rate using the Equations in § 63.1564(b)(4)(i) and you may use the alternative procedures in § 63.1573(a)(1) or (2) to determine Qr for those calculations

if you use the alternative procedure in § 63.1573(a)(1) only to demonstrate compliance with the inlet-velocity-to-primary-internal-cyclones requirement in § 63.1564(c)(5) then you must use that alternative procedure for both the performance test and for monitoring after the performance test

if you use either alternative in § 63.1573(a)(1) or (2) to determine exhaust gas flow then you must install, operate, and maintain the specified continuous parameter monitoring systems or, where allowed, determine and record hourly average volumetric air flow using the catalytic cracking unit control room instrumentation and must measure and record the gas temperature entering the control device as required in § 63.1573(a)(1)(i)–(iii) and § 63.1573(a)(2)(i)–(iii)

checklist: Is the unit a fluid catalytic cracking unit (FCC) regenerator vent at a petroleum refinery (i.e., the catalyst regeneration flue gas vent)?

Does the regenerator vent introduce any other gas streams (e.g., added oxygen-enriched air, nitrogen streams, or other gas feeds) into the catalyst regeneration vent, or is it limited to regenerator combustion gases (complete combustion unit)?
Have you elected which compliance option under § 63.1564(a)(1) you will use (e.g., NSPS Option 1a/1b/1c, Option 2, Option 3, or Option 4)?

Do you have (or can you install) the required continuous parameter monitoring system to measure and record the hourly average volumetric air flow to the regenerator OR can you reliably determine hourly average volumetric air flow from control room instrumentation as allowed in § 63.1573?

If relying on the gas-analyzer-based alternative, is a continuous gas analyzer installed in the regenerator exhaust vent prior to addition of any air or other gas streams and upstream of any CO boiler, and does it measure and record CO2, CO, and O2 as required?
Can you measure and record the temperature of the gas stream as near as practical to the control device or opacity monitor (or prior to a wet scrubber) as required by § 63.1573?

If you intend to use the alternative procedure only to demonstrate compliance with § 63.1564(c)(5) (inlet velocity to primary internal cyclones), will you use the alternative for both the performance test and for subsequent monitoring as required?

Do you have approval or will you seek approval from the permitting authority (or EPA/ delegated authority) to use the alternative monitoring procedure for compliance demonstrations that will be used in lieu of the NSPS equation and Method 2 for your NSPS-related performance test and ongoing monitoring?

judge_text: {"score":2,"reason":"EPA's key point—that Subpart UUU allows the alternative coke burn-off and regenerator exhaust flow procedures (with the conditions in §63.1573 and related provisions)—is reflected in the candidate subpart criteria and checklist (scope of regenerator vent, §63.1573(a)(1)/(2) options, monitoring/temperature and analyzer placement requirements, and use for performance test/ongoing monitoring)."}

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants for Petroleum Refineries (Refinery MACT)

criteria.criterion: If the plant site is a major source and contains petroleum refining process units that contain or contact HAPs listed in table 1, then Subpart CC applies to those petroleum refining process units and the related emission points at the plant site.

If a wastewater stream at a petroleum refinery has total annual benzene loading ≥ 10 megagrams per year, flow ≥ 0.02 liters per minute, benzene concentration ≥ 10 parts per million by weight, and is not exempt from control requirements under 40 CFR part 61 subpart FF, then that stream is a Group 1 wastewater stream under Subpart CC.

If a wastewater stream is designated Group 1 and is managed in a piece of equipment that is also subject to 40 CFR part 60 subpart QQQ, then after the Subpart CC compliance dates that stream is required to comply only with Subpart CC (i.e., not with NSPS subpart QQQ).

If a Group 1 wastewater stream or Group 2 stream is conveyed, stored, or treated in a wastewater management unit that also receives streams subject to subpart G wastewater provisions, then the stream must comply as specified in the §63.640(o)(2) alternatives (either the Part 61 subpart FF + subpart G combination or subpart G provisions), and that compliance constitutes compliance with Subpart CC for that stream.

candidates.title: Process Wastewater Provisions (Subpart G)

criteria.criterion: If a wastewater stream is also subject to 40 CFR part 61 subpart FF, then under Subpart G, after the Subpart G compliance dates the owner/operator is required to comply with the provisions of both Subpart G and part 61 subpart FF unless the owner/operator elects the alternative compliance options described in the subpart.

If an owner elects to designate a wastewater stream as Group 1 (rather than determine group status by measurement/calculation), then the owner must follow the designation procedures and the management/treatment requirements for Group 1 streams specified in §63.132(e) and the test/procedure requirements in §63.144.

If a wastewater stream meets the Group 1 criteria for Table 8 or Table 9 compounds (by concentration and/or flow rate per §63.132(c)–(d)), then it must be managed and treated under the applicable Group 1 performance standards in §63.138.

candidates.title: Cross-subpart Compliance Options (Subpart FFFF)

criteria.criterion: If a Group 1 or Group 2 wastewater stream is also subject to 40 CFR 61.342(c) through (h) and is not exempt under 40 CFR 61.342(c)(2) or (3), then under Subpart FFFF the owner/operator may elect to comply only with the Group 1 wastewater stream requirements in this subpart FFFF.

checklist: Verify that the plant site qualifies as a 'major source' under section 112(a) (determine applicability of Subpart CC) (40 CFR 63.640(a)).

Calculate total annual benzene for the wastewater stream using the procedures in 40 CFR 61.342 to confirm whether the stream meets the ≥10 megagrams/year threshold in the Group 1 definition (40 CFR 63.641).

Measure or determine the wastewater stream annual average flow rate and benzene concentration to confirm flow ≥ 0.02 L/min and benzene ≥ 10 ppmw required for Group 1 status (40 CFR 63.641; 40 CFR 63.144).

Determine whether the wastewater stream is exempt from control requirements under 40 CFR part 61 subpart FF (because Group 1 definition requires the stream to be 'not exempt' under subpart FF) (40 CFR 63.641).

If planning to designate a stream as Group 1 (rather than demonstrate by sampling/calculation), document the designation location and comply with the interim emission suppression requirements from the point of determination to the designation location per §63.132(e) and notify/record as required (40 CFR 63.132(e); 40 CFR 63.144).

Confirm whether the physical equipment (wastewater tanks, treatment unit, conveyance, or other management unit) that will manage this stream is also subject to 40 CFR part 60 subpart QQQ (NSPS QQQ); identify the specific unit(s) and their NSPS applicability (40 CFR 63.640(o)(1)).
Verify whether the Group 1 wastewater stream will be managed in equipment that also receives streams subject to Subpart G provisions (if so, follow the §63.640(o)(2) options) (40 CFR 63.640(o)(2)).

Confirm which compliance dates apply (Subpart CC compliance dates referenced in §63.640(h)) and whether the 'after the compliance dates' language in overlap provisions is in effect at your site (40 CFR 63.640(o)(1); 40 CFR 63.640(h)).

If you intend to control the stream under 40 CFR part 61 subpart FF (Benzene Waste Operations NESHAP), document whether that control approach creates an exemption or otherwise affects Group 1 status or overlap (because Group 1 definition references exemption under subpart FF and some overlap provisions reference part 61 subpart FF) (40 CFR 63.641; 40 CFR 63.110(e)).

If electing cross-subpart compliance options (for example per Subpart FFFF), identify and document the specific election in the Notification of Compliance Status and the provisions chosen to be used in lieu of other subparts (40 CFR 63.2535(j)).

candidates.title: Chemical Recovery Combustion Sources

criteria.criterion: If you are the owner or operator of an existing affected source or process unit, then you must comply with this subpart no later than March 13, 2004.

If your recovery furnace is subject to this subpart, then you must conduct an initial performance test and periodic performance tests using the test methods and procedures listed in § 63.7 and § 63.865(b), and tests must represent normal operating conditions (excluding startup, shutdown, and malfunctions).

If you seek to demonstrate compliance with the PM limits for recovery furnaces under § 63.862(a)(1)(i) or the alternative overall PM approach under § 63.862(a)(1)(ii), then you must use the procedures, corrections, sampling times/volumes, and Methods specified in § 63.865(b) (including Method 5, Method 29, or Method 17 with specified adjustments, minimum 60 minute/0.90 dscm runs, oxygen corrections and Method 3A/3B for oxygen).

candidates.title: Ore Crushing and Handling (initial test timing example provision)

criteria.criterion: If initial performance tests are required for an affected source under that subpart, then performance tests conducted between October 30, 2003 and no later than 180 days after the corresponding compliance date can be used for initial compliance demonstration provided the tests meet the initial performance testing requirements of that subpart.

candidates.title: Test Methods and Procedures for Pulp and Paper Sources

criteria.criterion: If you perform performance testing for pulp/paper-related sources, then you must conduct a minimum of three test runs representative of normal conditions with a minimum sampling time of 1 hour per run and average the results using the methods specified in § 63.457(b)(5) (e.g., Method 308, Method 320, Method 5/29/17 where applicable) and follow the vent sampling, port selection, flow, moisture, and run-count procedures in § 63.457(b).

If the Administrator requests or specifies conditions for performance tests, then tests must be conducted under such representative conditions as the Administrator specifies and records must be made available to the Administrator on request.

candidates.title: Stationary Combustion Turbines (initial test reuse criteria example)

criteria.criterion: If a previously conducted performance test is to be used in lieu of an initial test, then the prior test must have been conducted using the same methods specified in the subpart, must not be older than 2 years, must be reviewed and accepted by the Administrator, must have no process or equipment changes since the test (or you must demonstrate the test still reliably demonstrates compliance), and must have been conducted at a load within ±10 percent of 100 percent load.

checklist: Record the exact date(s) of the November 2003 particulate emission test(s) and compare to the Subpart MM compliance date (March 13, 2004) and any applicable 180-day windows referenced in other subparts.

Confirm the test methods actually used (e.g., Method 5, Method 29, or Method 17 with the specified adjustments) and that Method 17 adjustments (add 0.009 g/dscm and stack temperature ≤205 °C) and use of water as cleanup solvent (if required) were followed per 40 CFR 63.865(b)(1).

Verify each test run duration and sample volume (minimum 60 minutes and 0.90 dscm (31.8 dscf) per run) and confirm at least the minimum number of runs as required by applicable test-methoding provisions.

Document that the test runs were representative of normal operating conditions (not during startup, shutdown, or malfunction) and retain process records used to support representativeness as required by 40 CFR 63.865.
Confirm that oxygen concentration and volumetric flow were measured and corrected using the procedures/equations and Methods 3A/3B (or ANSI/ASME alternative) as required by 40 CFR 63.865(b)(2)-(4).

Verify that black liquor solids firing rate (BLS) and any CaO production rates used in calculations were measured using process data during the test as required by 40 CFR 63.865(b)(6) and § 63.865(a) calculation procedures if using overall PM approach.

Check whether the test report contains required sampling port/traverse selection, velocity/flow, moisture, and gas analysis documentation per Method 1/1A, Method 2 series, Method 4, and Method 3 series as referenced in 40 CFR 63.865(b)(5).

Determine whether the November 2003 tests were submitted to and reviewed/accepted by the Administrator (EPA) or delegated authority, or whether you need to request acceptance—RRRRR and YYYY-style provisions require Administrator review/acceptance for reuse of prior tests.

Confirm there have been no changes to control devices, air pollution control systems, or process equipment since the November 2003 test that would affect representativeness or require reestablishment of limits per 40 CFR 63.862(a)(1)(ii)(D).
Ensure the test report and supporting records are available to make available to the Administrator upon request (as required by 40 CFR 63.865 and 40 CFR 63.457(o)).

If relying on reuse-of-test precedents from other subparts, verify each applicable subpart's specific reuse criteria (e.g., tests not older than 2 years, same methods, Administrator acceptance, no process/equipment changes) and whether those criteria were met for your November 2003 test.
