candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants for Catalytic Cracking Units (Subpart UUU)

criteria.criterion: If you operate a catalytic cracking unit (FCCU) you must comply with the emission limitations and site-specific operating limits in this subpart and include the control device parameters and established operating limits in your operation, maintenance, and monitoring plan, and you must notify the Administrator if you elect to change the monitoring option for a specific control device that may be monitored using more than one continuous parameter monitoring system

If your FCCU regenerator vent uses a wet scrubber for PM control and is subject to the NSPS PM limit (per the NSPS provisions referenced in this subpart), then you may request approval to use alternative monitoring methods in lieu of the CPMS requirements under this subpart provided you meet the conditions and submit the required monitoring plan and approved NSPS alternative monitoring documentation

If you operate a wet scrubber of the jet ejector type or a scrubber equipped with atomizing spray nozzles, then you may use the daily air or water pressure check alternative instead of a continuous pressure-drop CPMS, maintain records of each check, and repair faulty lines within 12 hours of an abnormal reading

If you use continuous parameter monitoring systems and wish to set or adjust operating limits based on performance test results, then you must base operating limits on the performance test and you may (with limits) adjust one monitored operating parameter (flow rate, total power and secondary current, pressure drop, or liquid-to-gas ratio) from the performance-test average to a representative maximum (or minimum) worst-case value with supporting documentation, except that adjustment of equilibrium-catalyst Ni concentration has special restrictions

If you intend to monitor parameters other than those specified in this subpart (or otherwise need alternate monitoring), then you must request approval from the Administrator and include the description, demonstration methods, supporting calculations, monitoring frequency, and averaging time as specified in this subpart

If you want to change an established operating limit for a CPMS after the initial limit is set, then you may do so only by performing an additional performance test, a performance test with an engineering assessment, or an engineering assessment to verify compliance at the new operating limit and submit the revised limit as required

candidates.title: General monitoring requirements for control and recovery devices (Subpart SS)

criteria.criterion: If you are an owner or operator of a regulated source required to monitor under a referencing subpart, then you must install, calibrate, maintain, and operate CPMS according to manufacturer's specifications or other written procedures providing adequate assurance of accurate monitoring and ensure immediate repair or replacement of routine CPMS malfunctions

If your source is required to monitor, then you must establish a range for monitored parameters that indicates proper operation of the control device and submit the information required to establish that range in the Notification of Compliance Status or operating permit application/amendment

If you wish to monitor a different parameter than those established in the referencing subpart, then you may request approval to monitor a different parameter or to set unique monitoring parameters as specified by the referencing subpart procedures

candidates.title: Continuous monitoring requirements for wet scrubbers (Subpart TTTTT)

criteria.criterion: If a wet scrubber is subject to the operating limits for pressure drop and scrubber water flow rates specified in the referenced subpart, then you must at all times monitor the hourly average pressure drop and liquid flow rate using a CPMS according to the applicable CPMS requirements

candidates.title: Monitoring requirements for control devices (scrubbers) (Subpart OOO)

criteria.criterion: If you use a scrubber to comply with the requirements of this subpart, then you must install a pH monitoring device with a continuous recorder to monitor scrubber effluent pH and a flow measurement device with a continuous recorder at the scrubber influent and determine gas stream flow by one of the listed methods (design blower capacity, prior L/G determination, or an approved gas stream flow determination plan)

If you use a control device listed in this subpart but want to monitor a parameter other than those specified, then you must request approval to monitor alternative parameters according to the subpart's procedures

checklist: Confirm that the unit in question is a catalytic cracking unit (FCCU) subject to Subpart UUU and identify the specific regenerator vent(s).
Verify whether the FCCU regenerator vent is controlled by a wet scrubber and determine the scrubber type (e.g., jet ejector, atomizing spray nozzles, other).

Determine whether the FCCU regenerator vent is subject to the NSPS PM limit referenced in this subpart (see 63.1573(g)(1)(i)) and whether you have any NSPS-approved alternative monitoring for continuous opacity (40 CFR 60.105(a)(1)).
List the specific parameters currently monitored for the wet scrubber (pressure drop, liquid flow, liquid-to-gas ratio, pH, alkalinity, gas flow, opacity, CO, etc.) and the CPMS/equipment used.

Locate the site-specific operating limits established from the original performance test(s) for the monitored parameters and document the basis (performance test results, engineering assessment, manufacturer specs) used to set them.

If proposing adjusted parametric limits, prepare supporting documentation: performance test data, engineering assessment or calculations, and rationale showing worst-case representative conditions per §63.1571(d) and (e).

Determine whether the scrubber is subject to any other subpart monitoring mandates (e.g., requirements to monitor pressure drop and liquid flow with CPMS under a referencing subpart such as the one citing §63.9890(b)) and gather those citations/permit requirements.

Check whether you must include the change in your Notification of Compliance Status or submit the revised OM&M plan to the permitting authority before operating under new monitoring parameters (per §63.1574(f) and §63.1564(a)(2)).

If relying on the daily pressure-check alternative for pressure drop, confirm the scrubber qualifies (jet ejector or atomizing spray nozzles) and document daily check procedures, recordkeeping, and repair timelines (identify responsible personnel to repair within 12 hours).

Identify whether you must or will request Administrator approval to monitor alternative parameters (prepare the information required by §63.1573(f): description, demonstration methods, supporting calculations, monitoring frequency, averaging time).

candidates.title: Monitoring requirements

criteria.criterion: If you operate a steel pickling facility or acid regeneration plant subject to this subpart and you use a wet scrubber as the emission control device, then you must install, operate, and maintain systems to measure and continuously monitor and record the scrubber makeup water flow rate and, if applicable, recirculation water flow rate, with recordings at least once per shift while the scrubber is operating.

If you use a wet scrubber to achieve compliance, then during the performance test you must establish site-specific operating parameter values for the minimum scrubber makeup water flow rate (and minimum recirculation flow rate for scrubbers with recirculation) and monitor those parameters continuously during the test with recordings at least once every 15 minutes to determine compliant operating values.
If you wish to implement alternative monitoring requirements in lieu of the monitoring specified for wet scrubbers, then you may only do so with approval by the Administrator.

candidates.title: Control device and alternative work practice provisions

criteria.criterion: If a control device is used to comply with an applicable subpart that references §63.11, then monitoring equipment for that control device must be installed, calibrated, maintained, and operated according to the manufacturer's specifications or other written procedures that provide adequate assurance of accurate monitoring.

If an applicable subpart requires monitoring with a 40 CFR part 60, appendix A-7, Method 21 monitor, then you may elect to use the alternative work practice (optical gas imaging) instead of Method 21 provided you follow the requirements in §63.11(c) through (e).

candidates.title: Monitoring installation, operation, and maintenance requirements

criteria.criterion: If you are required by this subpart to monitor an operating parameter using a continuous monitoring system (CMS), then you must operate the CMS and collect data at all times the process is operating, collect data from at least four equally spaced periods each hour, have valid data for at least 75 percent of operating hours, and calculate hourly and daily averages as specified.

If you seek to monitor parameters other than those specified for scrubber control devices under this subpart, then you must request approval under §63.8(f) and submit a site-specific monitoring plan that (1) identifies the operating parameter to be monitored, (2) discusses why the parameter is appropriate for demonstrating ongoing compliance, and (3) identifies the specific monitoring procedures.

candidates.title: Monitoring alternatives and application content

criteria.criterion: If you request approval to monitor alternative parameter(s) rather than those specified in a subpart, then your request to the Administrator must include a description of each affected source and the parameter(s) to be monitored, a description of methods and procedures to demonstrate the parameter determines continuous compliance (including schedule), a certification that an operating limit representing compliant conditions will be established, the frequency and content of monitoring/recording/reporting, supporting calculations, and the averaging time for the alternative operating parameter.

checklist: Confirm the facility is a steel pickling facility or acid regeneration plant that is subject to Subpart CCC
Confirm the control device for the pickle line is a wet scrubber used to control HCl emissions

Verify current monitoring: do you continuously measure and record scrubber makeup water flow rate (and recirculation flow rate if applicable) with recordings at least once per shift while scrubber operates, and are those devices certified to ±5% and calibrated at least annually as required?

Obtain and review the most recent performance test(s) used to establish compliant operating parameters and confirm the site-specific minimum makeup water flow (and recirculation flow) established during those tests and the measurement frequency (≥ every 15 minutes during test)

Determine whether your proposed conductivity measurement correlates to the established performance-test-based operating limit(s) (i.e., demonstrate conductivity-to-HCl control relationship with test data)

Prepare a monitoring plan / alternative monitoring request for the Administrator per §63.8(f) and §63.1573(f) that includes: description of source and parameter, rationale why conductivity demonstrates compliance, test results demonstrating equivalence, proposed operating limit(s) tied to performance test conditions, monitoring frequency, data averaging time, supporting calculations, and O&M requirements

Confirm your monitoring system can meet CMS data requirements if applicable (collect data at ≥4 equally spaced periods/hour, provide valid data for ≥75% of operating hours, calculate hourly and daily averages as required)
Be prepared to demonstrate that the alternative monitoring will be implemented only after Administrator approval and retain records of the approval and supporting demonstration

Verify whether other subparts or permit conditions applicable to your source require specific scrubber monitoring parameters (e.g., pH, liquid flow) that could affect acceptability of conductivity as an alternative

candidates.title: Process vents — Polyvinyl chloride production (Subpart HHHHHHH)

criteria.criterion: If you use an absorber or acid gas scrubber to meet an emission limit in this subpart and are required to use a continuous parametric monitoring system (CPMS), then you must install and operate pressure gauges at the inlet and outlet to monitor the pressure drop through the scrubber.

If you seek to use an alternative monitoring parameter or procedure (for example, substituting ambient pressure for measured outlet pressure), then you must request and obtain approval from the Administrator as specified in this subpart and in the referenced notification/approval procedures, and until approval is granted you remain subject to the specified monitoring requirements.

If you establish or propose an alternative monitored parameter, then the operating limit for that parameter must be based on operating parameter values recorded during a performance test (and may be supplemented by engineering assessments or manufacturer recommendations) and must be included with the notification of compliance status or operating permit application.

candidates.title: General monitoring requirements for control and recovery devices (Subpart SS)

criteria.criterion: If you are an owner or operator required to monitor under this subpart, then monitoring must be conducted as set forth in this subpart unless the Administrator approves minor methodology changes or approves use of alternatives to monitoring requirements and procedures.

If you want to use alternatives to the continuous operating parameter monitoring or to monitor a different parameter than those established under the applicable referencing subpart, then you may request approval as provided in paragraph (d) of this section.

If you install CPMS, then the equipment must be installed, calibrated, maintained, and operated according to manufacturer's specifications or other written procedures that provide adequate assurance of accurate monitoring and must be operated in a manner consistent with good air pollution control practices.

candidates.title: Process vent provisions — monitoring requirements (Subpart G)

criteria.criterion: If you use a scrubber with an incinerator, boiler, or process heater to control halogenated vent streams, then you must install a pH monitoring device for effluent and a liquid flow meter at the scrubber influent and determine gas flow by one of the specified procedures (including using design blower capacity with appropriate adjustments for pressure drop).

If you seek to monitor a parameter other than those listed in this section, then you may request approval to monitor alternative parameters as provided in this section and by following the referenced subpart procedures.

candidates.title: Monitoring and inspection requirements (Subpart MMM)

criteria.criterion: If you are using a liquid scrubber under this subpart, then you must establish a minimum scrubber liquid flow rate or a minimum pressure drop as a site-specific operating parameter and measure and record that parameter at least once every 15 minutes with a monitoring device certified to the specified accuracy and calibrated annually.

If you want approval to monitor parameters other than those required by this section, then you may request approval to monitor alternative parameters according to the procedures specified in § 63.8(f) or in the Precompliance report as allowed by this subpart.

checklist: Identify whether the scrubber in question is an absorber or acid gas scrubber used to comply with emission limits under Subpart HHHHHHH (i.e., controls process vents subject to Table 1 or 2 of that subpart).
Determine whether CPMS use is required for that control device under § 63.11925(c) (i.e., whether the scrubber is among devices that must have continuous parametric monitoring).
Document the current monitored parameter, sensor locations (inlet and outlet), and whether the system currently measures inlet pressure and outlet pressure to compute pressure drop.
Collect the sensor specifications: accuracy, manufacturer certification (±10% where applicable), calibration frequency, and installation location and procedures.

Assemble performance test records (initial compliance performance test and any subsequent tests) showing the operating parameter values during demonstration that the control device met the emission limits.
Prepare engineering rationale showing how ambient pressure (the proposed alternative) would provide a representative and equivalent measure of pressure drop compared with measured outlet pressure.

Locate and assemble any prior approval(s) you received for the similar request for the other scrubber (approval letter, approving authority, scope and conditions) and note whether approval was from EPA or the delegated Texas authority.

Verify the appropriate approval route and recipient: under Subpart HHHHHHH submit the alternative-monitoring request per §§ 63.11985(c)(4)/(5) (and follow § 63.8 procedures) and confirm whether the Texas delegated authority or EPA Administrator is the approver.

Prepare the monitoring-plan elements required by § 63.11935(c)(1) (performance criteria/design specs, sampling interface location, QA/QC, operation/maintenance, reporting) showing the proposed alternative parameter and why it indicates proper operation.

Determine and document the proposed operating limit for the alternative parameter based on performance test data and engineering assessment and be ready to include the rationale and calculations in the Notification of Compliance Status or permit application per § 63.11935(d)(2).

Confirm data acquisition requirements (minimum 15-minute recording and data resolution/accuracy per § 63.11935(c)(2) and (6)) and that the proposed alternative monitoring can meet those recording/accuracy/resolution requirements.

Confirm that until formal approval is granted you will continue to operate and report under the existing monitoring requirements (do not implement the alternative parameter for compliance until approval is received).

Identify any bypass lines, flow indicators, or other relevant system elements that could affect representativeness of pressure measurements and verify that CPMS installation locations would provide representative measurements per § 63.11935(c)(1)(ii) and 63.996(c)(4).

Prepare the justification information described in § 63.11985(c)(4) and (5): description of the proposed alternative, technical/economic impracticality if applicable, and the methods/procedures to demonstrate the parameter indicates proper operation, including frequency of measurements and proposed operating limits.

candidates.title: Subpart LLLLLL - Standards and compliance requirements for acrylonitrile polymerization and monomer recovery

criteria.criterion: If you use a wet scrubber to control polymerization process equipment, then you must maintain the daily average water flow rate to that wet scrubber at a minimum of 50 liters per minute and operate a CPMS that records flow at least every 15 minutes and records daily averages.

If you use a wet scrubber to control monomer recovery process equipment, then you must maintain the daily average water flow rate to that wet scrubber at a minimum of 30 liters per minute and operate a CPMS that records flow at least every 15 minutes and records daily averages.

If you do not use a wet scrubber control device for the polymerization or monomer recovery process equipment, then you must submit an EPA‑approved monitoring plan that includes device description, test results per §63.1104 of subpart YY, an O&M plan and CPMS, monitored operating parameters, and operating parameter limits based on a performance test.

If you seek to change the wet scrubber operating limits, then you must notify the Administrator, conduct a new performance test demonstrating compliance with the applicable emissions limits, and establish revised operating limits using CPMS measurements collected during the performance test.

candidates.title: Subpart SS - General monitoring requirements for control and recovery devices

criteria.criterion: If you are an owner or operator of a regulated source required to monitor under this subpart, then you must conduct monitoring as set forth in this subpart and the relevant referencing subpart unless the Administrator specifies or approves minor methodological changes or approves alternatives to monitoring requirements.

If you want to use alternatives to the continuous operating parameter monitoring and recordkeeping provisions or to monitor a different parameter than those established in the subpart, then you may request Administrator approval as provided in this section.

If you use a CPMS, then you must install, calibrate, maintain, and operate monitoring equipment according to manufacturer specifications or other written procedures, ensure timely repair of routine malfunctions, and verify operational status prior to or in conjunction with performance tests.

candidates.title: Subpart HHHHHHH - CPMS requirements for control devices for process vents

criteria.criterion: If you are required to use CPMS for a control device that meets process vent emission limits and you are using an absorber or acid gas scrubber, then you must install a flow meter to monitor scrubber influent liquid flow and either (i) monitor liquid flow only or (ii) monitor liquid flow and gas flow so you can determine and record the liquid‑to‑gas ratio consistent with the performance test.

If you use an absorber or acid gas scrubber and the scrubbing liquid is a reactant, then you must install and operate a pH, caustic strength, or conductivity monitoring device for the scrubber effluent.

If you wish to use alternative monitoring parameters or procedures for CPMS required by this subpart, then you may request Administrator approval to use alternatives as specified in the subpart's alternative monitoring provisions.

candidates.title: Subpart UUU - Monitoring alternatives (examples and application procedures)

criteria.criterion: If you operate a jet ejector type wet scrubber or a wet scrubber equipped with atomizing spray nozzles, then you may use daily checks of the air or water pressure to the spray nozzles, maintain records of each daily check, and repair or replace faulty lines within 12 hours as an alternative to continuous pressure‑drop CPMS.

If you wish to use other alternative monitoring parameters or systems (including automated data compression or other parameters), then you must submit a written request to the Administrator including descriptions, demonstration methods, monitoring frequency, supporting calculations, and averaging time as specified in the rule.

If you propose an alternative monitoring method that will be used to demonstrate compliance, then you must submit the application by the deadlines specified (e.g., with the site‑specific test plan or at least 60 days before the performance evaluation) and the Administrator will notify intent to deny within 60 days or the method is deemed approved.

checklist: Determine whether your facility's polymerization and monomer recovery operations are subject to Subpart LLLLLL (acrylonitrile polymerization/monomer recovery) and identify which emission points are process vents controlled by scrubbers.
Identify whether the scrubber(s) controlling AN emissions are wet scrubbers and whether they control polymerization process equipment or monomer recovery process equipment.
Measure and document current daily average water flow rates to each wet scrubber and whether you have CPMS that records flow at least every 15 minutes and computes daily averages.

If you do not use a wet scrubber for a given control point, assemble the monitoring plan contents required by 63.11395(i)(1)–(5) (device description, performance test results per §63.1104 subpart YY, O&M plan, list of monitored parameters, and operating limits based on performance test).
Determine whether any scrubber is a jet ejector or uses atomizing spray nozzles (the design/type that 63.1573(b) addresses).

Inventory existing monitoring hardware and procedures (pressure gauges, flow meters, pH probes, conductivity/caustic strength monitors, data logging frequency) and confirm they meet the specific instrument/location requirements cited in the applicable subpart.

Decide which parameter(s) you would propose to monitor instead of the standard parameter (e.g., pressure checks, pH strip/titration, liquid flow only, liquid‑to‑gas ratio), and prepare supporting demonstrations/calculations showing these correlate with control performance.

Prepare a draft alternative‑monitoring request with the information required (description of source and parameters, methods/procedures to demonstrate parameter validity, monitoring/recording/reporting frequency and rationale, supporting calculations, and averaging time) per 63.1573(f) / applicable subpart procedures.

If seeking revised scrubber operating limits based on performance testing, plan to (a) notify Administrator, (b) conduct a performance test demonstrating compliance with emission limits, and (c) collect CPMS measurements during test runs to set revised limits as specified in 63.11395(k).

Confirm recordkeeping and reporting capabilities to retain monthly/quarterly summaries and daily/15‑minute CPMS records as required by the applicable subpart(s) and to provide prompt written notification of any exceedance as required.

candidates.title: Taconite Iron Ore Processing NESHAP (operating limits and monitoring for wet and dynamic wet scrubbers)

criteria.criterion: If you operate a dynamic wet scrubber at a taconite affected source to meet any particulate matter emission limit in Table 1, then you must maintain the daily average scrubber water flow rate and the daily average fan amperage (as a surrogate for fan speed) at or above the minimum levels established during the initial performance test and monitor those parameters with a CPMS.

If you operate any wet scrubber (including dynamic wet scrubbers subject to alternative earlier requirements), then you must meet the applicable operating limits for pressure drop and scrubber water flow rate (or fan amperage where allowed) established during the initial performance test and follow continuous compliance and corrective action procedures when daily averages fall below those limits.

candidates.title: Monitoring provisions for kraft/soda recovery furnaces and related wet scrubbers (CPMS and alternative fan-amperage methods)

criteria.criterion: If you seek to set minimum scrubber fan operating limits using percent full load amperage (PFLA) for dynamic (no-load) type scrubbers as an alternative to pressure drop, then the minimum PFLA must be set as the percent of full load amperage under no-load, plus 10 percent, with the no-load amperage determined from manufacturer specifications or by performing a no-load test.

If you seek to set minimum fan-amperage operating limits using alternative methods allowed under this subpart, then you must use the specified procedures (e.g., midpoint between lowest test-run amperage and no-load, or PFLA method) and ensure monitors meet the CPMS accuracy/measurement frequency requirements.

candidates.title: Procedure to change compliance levels of monitored parameters (approval and additional performance testing)

criteria.criterion: If you want to change or expand control device or process operating parameter levels established during performance tests, then you must notify the Administrator and, upon approval, conduct additional performance tests at the proposed new parameter levels to verify you still meet the applicable emission limits before operating at those new levels.

candidates.title: Standards and test procedures for wet scrubbers (site-specific operating limits for pressure drop and liquid flow rate)

criteria.criterion: If your wet scrubber is subject to operating limits for pressure drop and scrubber liquid flow rate under this subpart, then you must establish site-specific operating limits by measuring and recording pressure drop and scrubbing liquid flow at least every 15 minutes during each run of the particulate matter performance test and set the operating limits as the lowest average values from the test runs.

checklist: Confirm that your facility is an 'affected source' under Subpart RRRRR (taconite ore processing) and that the twelve dynamic wet scrubbers are used to meet particulate matter emission limits in Table 1 to that subpart.

Determine the construction/reconstruction dates of the affected sources relative to the dates in the RRRRR provisions (e.g., commenced construction or reconstruction on or before 9/25/2019; after 7/28/2020) to know which monitoring requirements and dates (e.g., 1/28/2022) apply.

Verify whether an initial performance test has been performed for each dynamic wet scrubber and whether the test measured scrubber water flow rate and fan amperage (or pressure drop) at 15-minute intervals per the CPMS procedures.

Verify that a CPMS is installed, operated, and maintained for each dynamic wet scrubber and that it records the required parameters at the required frequency (every 15 minutes) and with required accuracy.
Obtain the fan motor full-load amperage (FLA) and no-load amperage values from manufacturer specifications or conduct a no-load test for each fan motor to support any PFLA calculation.

Calculate the candidate PFLA values using the no-load and full-load amperage data (per 63.864(e)(10)(iii)(2)) and compare with the lowest average fan amperage values measured during compliant performance test runs to see if the proposed PFLA method would set the same or different minimum operating limit.

Decide whether you will request Administrator approval or submit a petition/site-specific monitoring plan or a request to change operating limits (per Subpart DDD and RRRRR) and prepare to notify/seek approval and, if required, conduct additional performance testing to demonstrate compliance at the proposed new parameter levels.

Check Title V permit testing schedule and reporting requirements (e.g., subsequent performance tests) to ensure any revised operating limits and monitoring approaches are consistent with permit conditions.
Prepare to implement corrective action and recordkeeping procedures required when daily averages fall below established operating limits (per 40 CFR 63.9634(l)/(f)(4)).

candidates.title: Surface Coating of Automobile and Light-Duty Trucks

criteria.criterion: If you obtain approval to use results of a previously conducted transfer efficiency test and the previous test was conducted using the methods and conditions specified in this subpart, then you are not required to conduct a new transfer efficiency test.

If either no process or equipment changes have been made since the previous test or you can demonstrate that the previous test results reliably demonstrate compliance despite any changes, then you may use the previous transfer efficiency test results instead of performing a new test.

If the previous test either established the required operating parameters or collected sufficient data to establish the required operating parameters, then you may use the previous test results in lieu of a new transfer efficiency test.

If you cannot produce the required supporting documentation and records showing the previous transfer efficiency test methods, raw data, representative operating conditions, and any operating parameters needed to demonstrate compliance, then you cannot rely on the previous test results without Administrator approval.

checklist: Confirm the exact date of the previous transfer efficiency test and retrieve the complete test report and raw data (Dec 2004).
Verify the test method used for transfer efficiency (e.g., ASTM D5066-91 or EPA-453/R-08-002) and that the method matches §63.3161(g).

Document which coatings were tested and whether the tested coatings were representative of current primer-surfacer and topcoat formulations and the spray booths tested (representative coatings/booths).
Confirm the test was conducted under representative operating conditions and check records showing process conditions during the test (run durations, production runs), per §63.3164(a)(1).

Verify whether the previous test established the required operating parameters (transfer efficiency values and any parameters used to set operating limits) or contains sufficient data to establish them.

Inventory any process or equipment changes since the test (spray equipment, booth enclosures, curing/flash-off arrangements, capture systems) and document whether changes could affect transfer efficiency.
Assemble and retain all records and calculations required by §63.3130, including raw data, algorithms, intermediate calculations, and panel test documentation if used.
If any of the above checks fail or uncertainty remains, prepare and submit a request to the Administrator for approval to use the previous test results, with supporting demonstration per §63.3160(c).

candidates.title: Subpart NNNNN

criteria.criterion: If you are required by §63.9020(e) to monitor operating parameters for a scrubber control device, then you must install, operate, and maintain each continuous monitoring system (CMS) and collect data at the frequencies and averaging methods specified in §63.9025(a).

If you use a scrubber control device and want to monitor parameters other than those specified in §63.9020(e), then you may request approval under §63.8(f) by submitting a site-specific monitoring plan that (1) identifies the operating parameter, (2) explains why it is appropriate to demonstrate ongoing compliance, and (3) identifies specific monitoring procedures as required by §63.9025(b).

If you use a caustic scrubber or a water scrubber to meet the emission limits in Table 1 to this subpart, then you must keep records of the daily average scrubber inlet liquid or recirculating liquid flow rate and the daily average scrubber effluent pH as specified in §63.9035(b).

candidates.title: Subpart HHHHHHH

criteria.criterion: If you are using an absorber or acid gas scrubber to meet an emission limit in Table 1 or 2 to this subpart and are required to use CPMS under §63.11925(c), then you must install and operate the monitoring equipment specified in §63.11940(c)(1)–(3) (for example, a liquid influent flow meter, pressure gauges for pressure drop, and pH/caustic strength/conductivity monitoring where the scrubbing liquid is reactive).

If you wish to propose alternative monitoring parameters or procedures for a control device covered by this section, then you may request approval to use alternatives to the continuous operating parameter monitoring listed in this section as specified in §63.11940(h)(1)–(2).

candidates.title: Subpart G

criteria.criterion: If you use a recovery device or recapture device and an absorber is the final recovery device in the recovery system to comply with the process vent requirements, then you must use a scrubbing liquid temperature monitoring device and a specific gravity monitoring device each equipped with a continuous recorder as specified in §63.114(a)(5)(ii).

If you seek to monitor parameters other than those listed in paragraph (a) or (b) of §63.114 for a process vent control or recovery device, then you may request approval to monitor different parameters under §63.114(c) following the applicable approval procedures for this subpart.

candidates.title: Subpart SS

criteria.criterion: If you are the owner or operator of a regulated source required to monitor under this subpart, then you must install, operate, and maintain CPMS and related monitoring per the general requirements in §63.996(c) and establish parameter ranges that indicate proper operation per §63.996(c)(6).

If you want to monitor a different parameter than those listed for establishing proper operation or to set unique monitoring parameters under this subpart, then you may request approval to monitor a different parameter or set unique monitoring parameters as provided in §63.996(d)(2).

checklist: Identify which specific 40 CFR part 63 subpart and table/section establishes the HCl emission limit you must meet (which subpart requires the scrubber as a control or recovery device).
Confirm whether the scrubber is operated as a control device to meet an emission limit or as a recovery/recapture device (i.e., final recovery device/absorber) for a process vent.
Determine whether the scrubber scrubbing medium is a caustic scrubber, a water scrubber, or a reactive scrubbing liquid (affects whether pH/caustic strength/conductivity monitoring is required).
Determine whether your source is subject to CPMS/continuous monitoring requirements under the applicable subpart (e.g., requirement to install CPMS per referenced subpart).

Verify whether initial performance testing has been performed and which operating parameters (flow, pH, temperature, L/G ratio, etc.) and operating limits were established during that performance test.

Decide which alternative parameter(s) you propose to monitor (e.g., scrubber base temperature, liquid flow indicators) and prepare a rationale tying those parameters to maintaining the control/capture efficiency measured in the initial performance test.

Prepare a monitoring plan per §63.8(f) (or the subpart-specific plan requirements) that: identifies the parameter(s), explains why they demonstrate ongoing compliance, specifies monitoring procedures/frequency/averaging, and describes data recording and QA/QC consistent with §63.9025(a) or subpart-specific monitoring rules.

Confirm the proposed monitoring frequency and data-availability/averaging approach meets the referenced subpart's CMS/CPMS data collection and averaging requirements (e.g., 4 equally spaced periods per hour, hourly/daily averages) or propose an adequate alternative in the plan.

List the records you will keep (e.g., daily average inlet/recirculating liquid flow rate, daily average effluent pH, inspections/calibrations) and the retention/ reporting approach required by the applicable subpart.

If the scrubber is functioning as a recovery device, verify whether scrubbing liquid temperature and specific gravity (or other recovery-device parameters) are required and whether you will propose alternatives to those parameters.
Confirm whether any manufacturer certifications/calibrations or accuracy requirements apply to monitoring devices per the applicable subpart and schedule for calibration/maintenance.

Be prepared to establish operating limits (ranges that indicate proper operation) based on performance test results and to submit those ranges in the Notification of Compliance Status or permit application as required by the applicable subpart.

If you will rely on alternative monitoring, prepare supporting calculations and demonstration data showing the proposed parameter(s) reliably indicate proper operation (as required by subpart-specific alternative-monitoring application procedures).

Determine the applicable Administrator approval pathway (§63.8(f) or subpart-specific procedures such as the sections referenced in §63.114(c), §63.1417(j), §63.11985, or other subpart procedural cross-references) and the submission package and timing for the request.

candidates.title: Ethylene Oxide Emissions Standards for Sterilization Facilities

criteria.criterion: If an aeration room vent (ARV) at your facility is an affected source subject to an emission standard in § 63.362 and your facility is required to monitor using EtO CEMS, then the ARV exhaust must be monitored with an EtO CEMS installed and operated in accordance with Appendix A to Subpart O and Performance Specification 19 (PS 19) (i.e., a certified EtO CEMS) and you must follow the QA/operation provisions in Appendix A and Procedure 7 of appendix F to part 60.

If your facility's total EtO use is less than 100 pounds per year, then you may demonstrate continuous compliance by periodic performance testing (and associated monitored operating limits) instead of installing and operating EtO CEMS for affected sources, per the applicability options in the rule.

If you are required to use an EtO CEMS to provide compliance data, then the monitoring system must be capable of measuring EtO mass emissions in lb/hr, be certified according to PS 19 (including the PS19 certification tests and section 13 certification), satisfy the Appendix A continuous operation and data reduction requirements (one cycle per 15 minutes, hourly averaging, conversion to lb/hr), and meet the ongoing QA/QC tests and reporting described in Appendix A.

If the instrument you propose (e.g., a gas detector) cannot be certified and shown to pass the certification and routine QA tests required by PS 19 and Appendix A (including LOD/SADL, interference testing, measurement error tests, daily/7‑day calibration drift or calibration error tests, quarterly audits/RAA or RATA as applicable), then it cannot be used to provide quality‑assured EtO concentration data for compliance reporting under this subpart.

If you plan to use a temporary like‑kind replacement analyzer or a non‑redundant backup EtO monitoring system at a unit or stack location, then you must complete the required calibration/linearity checks and QA tests when brought into service and you are limited to 720 hours per year of use at that location unless a RATA is performed and passed first.

If you instead are using a direct measurement instrument to determine sterilization chamber concentration (a chamber concentration direct‑measurement approach, which is distinct from monitoring ARV exhaust), then any instrument used must be identified in the monitoring plan and the monitoring plan must document the measurement principle, potential interferences, calibration procedures, and accuracy requirements for that instrument.

checklist: Confirm whether the aeration room vent (ARV) at your facility is an affected source under § 63.360(b)(2) and which emission standard(s) in § 63.362 apply.
Determine your facility's total EtO use (pounds per year) to see if the facility is in the <100 lb/yr alternative (§ 63.363, § 63.364(a)(2)).

If using EtO CEMS: obtain the ET‑6200R U spec sheet and verify whether the manufacturer or a testing authority has (or can provide) PS 19 certification, or evidence the unit can meet all PS 19 certification tests (section 13) and Appendix A certification/QA tests (LOD/SADL, interference, ME, calibration drift, RATA/RAA, CGA/DSA).

Verify the proposed analyzer's continuous sampling behavior: completes cycles at least once every 15 minutes and provides data averaged per Appendix A requirements (1‑min averaging or better and hourly averages computed per § 60.13(h)(2) as referenced).

Verify the proposed analyzer's measurement range, method detection limit (ppbv), and whether its detection limit is an order of magnitude below the concentration equivalent of the applicable emission limit (§ 63.365(b)(5)(i)(A)).
Obtain manufacturer's or third‑party interference test data and method detection/LOD/SADL test records (or plan to perform them) per Appendix A test requirements.

Confirm the analyzer can perform or support required QA procedures (daily/7‑day CD or calibration error tests, linearity checks, cylinder gas audits, dynamic spiking, ME tests, quarterly RAA/RATA) and that you can record all required test details per Appendix A (10.1.5.1.x).
Check whether you will need any flow, diluent gas, or moisture monitoring (part 75 devices) to convert concentration to lb/hr and plan for their certification and QA per Appendix A and part 75.

Decide whether the device will be primary, redundant backup, non‑redundant backup, or temporary like‑kind replacement and confirm the applicable limits and QA steps (e.g., 720‑hour limit for non‑redundant/temporary uses unless RATA passed).

Prepare or update the electronic and hard‑copy monitoring plan (Appendix A § 10.1.1.2) to identify the instrument model, measurement principle, potential interferences, calibration procedures, sample acquisition method, and procedures for certification and QA.

Confirm data acquisition, storage, and reporting capability (hourly ppbv recorded to required precision, conversion to lb/hr, and electronic reporting via CEDRI per Appendix A 11 and § 63.366/§ 63.Appendix A reporting requirements).

If you cannot certify the proposed sensor per PS19 or cannot demonstrate passing the required tests, plan for an alternative certified EtO CEMS (e.g., analyzers demonstrated under PS19/Method 320) or pursue an Administrator‑approved alternative under § 63.8(f) (note approval is retained by EPA per § 63.368(c)).

candidates.title: Subpart HH

criteria.criterion: If ancillary equipment or compressors located at a natural gas processing plant operate in VHAP service for 300 hours or more per calendar year, then they are subject to the equipment leak standards of this subpart.

If the percent VHAP content of the process fluid contained in or contacting a piece of ancillary equipment or a compressor can be reasonably expected never to exceed 10.0 percent by weight as determined using Method 18 or ASTM D6420-99 (2004) following the provisions of § 63.772(a)(1)(ii), then that piece of equipment is considered not in VHAP service (and not subject to VHAP-service provisions).
If a piece of ancillary equipment or compressor contains or contacts field gas prior to extraction of natural gas liquids, then it is considered to operate in wet gas service.

If any ancillary equipment and compressors contain or contact a fluid with a total VHAP concentration less than 10 percent by weight as determined according to § 63.772(a), then the owner or operator is exempt from the routine monitoring requirements referenced in § 63.764(c)(3) (i.e., the exemption in § 63.764(e)(2)(i) applies).

candidates.title: Subpart HHH

criteria.criterion: If you are determining glycol dehydration unit natural gas flowrate, benzene, or BTEX emissions, then you must determine flowrate using either a direct flow instrument (±2% accuracy) or documentation of annual average and determine benzene/BTEX using GRI-GLYCalc or direct measurement by Method 18 or ASTM D6420 (or an alternative approved method) as specified in § 63.1282(a).

If performing a no-detect leak test for interfaces under this subpart, then you must use Method 21 (40 CFR part 60, appendix A) and follow the calibration, instrument response factor (for average stream composition), and background adjustment provisions in § 63.1282(b).

candidates.title: Subpart EEEE

criteria.criterion: If you need to determine the HAP content of an organic liquid, then you may use Method 311, ASTM D6886-18 (using Method B or B with C as specified), or another Administrator‑approved method, and if the selected method reports a range you must use the upper end of the HAP content range for compliance calculations.

If you are using Method 18 or an alternative GC‑MS method to measure total organic HAP (TOC) or total organic compounds for control‑device performance, then ASTM D6420 may be used only when the target compounds match Section 1.1 and target concentrations are between 150 ppbv and 100 ppmv (or when the ASTM requirements in § 63.2354(b)(3)(ii) are otherwise met).

checklist: Confirm the facility is a natural gas processing plant (per the Subpart HH facility definition) and identify which units are within that affected source.

Identify and list each piece of equipment that meets the Subpart HH definition of ancillary equipment (pumps, PRDs, sampling connection systems, open-ended lines/valves, flanges/connectors) and all compressors (per 40 CFR 63.761).

For each piece of ancillary equipment and each compressor, determine whether the fluid it contains or contacts is field gas prior to NGL extraction (i.e., wet gas service) or is downstream/processed gas or liquid.

For each process fluid (gas or liquid) that contacts equipment, determine whether the percent VHAP (fraction by weight of all HAP) can be reasonably expected never to exceed 10.0% by weight; document the method(s) you will use to demonstrate that expectation (see options below).

If planning to use Method 18 (40 CFR part 60, appendix A) for gas streams, document sampling plan, target compounds list, sampling duration (minimum 1 hr or grab sample scheme as required elsewhere for performance tests), and laboratory analysis procedures.

If planning to use ASTM D6420 (note HH cites D6420‑99 (2004) while other subparts may reference later versions), verify that target compounds are listed in the ASTM method's Section 1.1 (or, for non‑listed compounds, that they are amenable to MS and that the additional continuing calibration check per § 63.772(a)(1)(ii)(C) will be performed and documented) and that target concentrations fall between 150 ppbv and 100 ppmv as required.

For liquid hydrocarbon streams, determine whether you will use Method 311 or ASTM D6886-18 (Method B or B with C) (or Administrator‑approved alternative) to quantify HAP content; if using SDS or product/spec data, document why those data are representative and be prepared to use an analytical method if requested by the Administrator.

Record and retain representative samples, sample handling procedures, and sampling plan (including number of samples and averaging period) to support the VHAP determination; ensure samples are collected and preserved to minimize volatilization and are representative of the stream.

For any equipment where you claim VHAP <10% and therefore not in VHAP service or exempt from monitoring, maintain records of the analysis, method used, dates, and justification so they are available for inspection (per Subpart HH recordkeeping requirements).

If using Method 21 for no‑detect determinations, ensure the portable instrument is calibrated daily with specified calibration gases (zero air and methane standard <10,000 ppmv), determine and document the instrument response factor for the average stream composition (inert‑free basis if inert gases present), and document whether you will adjust readings for background concentration.

Determine and document the number of operating hours per calendar year that each piece of equipment is in VHAP service (to verify the 300 hours/year applicability threshold for equipment leak standards).

For glycol dehydration units (if present), verify the natural gas flowrate measurement approach (direct meter ±2% or documented annual average) and whether benzene/BTEX emissions will be determined by GRI‑GLYCalc or by direct measurement using Method 18/ASTM D6420 per § 63.1282(a).
If relying on ASTM‑based GC‑MS methods, document that your laboratory can perform required continuing calibration checks and can detect/quantify the relevant compounds at the needed reporting limits.
Be prepared to use the upper bound of any reported HAP content ranges (per Subpart EEEE) when calculating total HAP/VHAP percentages for compliance determinations.

candidates.title: General Provisions (Subpart A)

criteria.criterion: If required to perform performance testing by a relevant standard and a force majeure event is about to occur, occurs, or has occurred that may cause a delay in testing beyond the regulatory deadline, then the owner or operator must notify the Administrator in writing as soon as practicable before the performance test deadline (unless delayed notice is itself delayed by the force majeure), provide a written description and rationale attributing the delay to the force majeure, describe measures taken to minimize the delay, identify a proposed test date, and await the Administrator's discretionary decision on any extension.

If the owner or operator is unable to conduct a scheduled performance test on the notified date due to unforeseeable circumstances beyond their control, then the owner or operator must notify the Administrator as soon as practicable and without delay prior to the scheduled test date and specify the rescheduled date.

If required to submit notifications or reports electronically via the EPA's electronic systems and a force majeure event prevents timely electronic submission within the applicable period, then you may assert a claim of force majeure by notifying the Administrator in writing as soon as possible and providing a written description, rationale, measures to minimize delay, and the date by which you propose to submit the notification or report; approval is at the Administrator's discretion.

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Iron and Steel Foundries (Subpart EEEEE)

criteria.criterion: If you are an iron and steel foundry subject to this subpart, then you must conduct a performance test to demonstrate initial compliance with each applicable emissions limitation no later than 180 calendar days after the compliance date specified in § 63.7683.

If initial compliance with work practice standards or operation and maintenance requirements (where initial compliance is not via a performance test) is required, then you must demonstrate initial compliance no later than 30 calendar days after the compliance date specified in § 63.7683.

If performance testing is delayed by a period of malfunction, then you may not conduct performance tests during the malfunction, must conduct tests under conditions representative of normal operations (excluding startup/shutdown/malfunction), and must record and be prepared to make available process information supporting that the test conditions represent normal operation.

If you seek to extend the initial performance test deadline for an iron and steel foundry due to force majeure, then you must follow the force majeure/extension procedures referenced in § 63.7(a)(2) and § 63.7(a)(4).

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Metal Melting Furnaces / Foundry Metal Melting Furnaces (Subpart ZZZZZ)

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate a metal melting furnace (or group of metal melting furnaces) subject to the emissions limits in § 63.10895(c), then you must conduct a performance test to demonstrate initial compliance within 180 days of your compliance date and report the results in your notification of compliance status.

If you own or operate an existing foundry and have prior PM or total metal HAP performance test results conducted within the last 5 years using the specified methods and no process changes (or you can demonstrate the prior results remain reliable despite changes), then you may submit those prior test results in lieu of a new performance test provided you notify the Administrator in writing of your intent to use prior data no later than 60 days after your compliance date.

If performance testing was delayed by furnace malfunction or other non-representative conditions, then you may not perform the test during the malfunction and must conduct each performance test under conditions representative of normal operations, record the necessary process information, and include an explanation supporting that those conditions represent normal operation.

checklist: Confirm which NESHAP subpart(s) the facility is subject to (e.g., Subpart EEEEE for iron and steel foundries, Subpart ZZZZZ for metal melting furnaces) and record the specific compliance date(s) from the applicable standard.
Determine whether initial performance testing is required for each emission unit and the regulatory deadline (typically 180 days after the compliance date) for each required test.
Document the date you first knew (or should have known through due diligence) that the event (furnace malfunction or labor strike) may cause a delay beyond the performance test deadline.

Assemble evidence that the event was beyond the control of the facility (e.g., maintenance records showing unexpected furnace failure, strike start date and impact on staffing/contractors) and whether it prevented timely testing.

If relying on prior performance tests in lieu of new tests (Subpart ZZZZZ option), verify that the prior test was conducted within 5 years, used the required methods, and that no process changes occurred (or prepare justification showing prior results remain reliable).

If required to submit notifications/reports electronically (CEDRI/CDX/ERT), verify the electronic submission requirement, the due dates, and whether the force majeure occurred within the period applicable to electronic submissions (see five business day window where specified).

Prepare the written notification to the Administrator as soon as practicable including: description of the event, rationale linking the event to delayed testing/submittal, measures taken or to be taken to minimize delay, and a proposed date to conduct the performance test or submit the report.

Verify whether a site-specific test plan has been submitted or approved and whether a 60-calendar-day notification of intent to test was provided (or if rescheduling notice is required under §63.7(b)(2)).

Record process data and a narrative explaining why candidate test conditions would NOT represent normal operation during the malfunction, and prepare documentation showing planned steps to resume normal operations and conduct the test as soon as practicable.

Retain copies of all notifications, correspondence with the Administrator, test plans, test scheduling notices, and evidence of attempts to minimize delay (at least 5 years as required for test records).

If you intend to assert force majeure for electronic submittals, compile dates/times of attempted electronic access, and any evidence that the force majeure prevented timely electronic submission (for EPA-system outages see the separate outage procedures).

Be prepared that approval of any deadline extension or force majeure claim is discretionary—document all efforts made to meet deadlines despite the event and any alternative measures taken (e.g., temporary repairs, alternative testing arrangements).

candidates.title: General Provisions

criteria.criterion: If the owner or operator wishes to use an alternative monitoring procedure (minor, intermediate, or major change) to the monitoring methods specified in the relevant standard, then the owner or operator must obtain the Administrator's approval by submitting an application that meets the requirements in § 63.8(f).

If a continuous monitoring system (CMS) is required by a relevant standard, then the CMS must be installed, operated, maintained, and performance-evaluated according to the provisions of § 63.8 (including operation/maintenance, QA, performance-evaluation plan submission, and data reduction requirements).

candidates.title: Cellulose Products Manufacturing

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate a cellulose products manufacturing operation located at a major source of HAP emissions, then Subpart UUUU applies to your facility.

If you use a CEMS to measure hydrogen sulfide emissions, then that CEMS must be installed, operated, and maintained according to Performance Specification PS-7 (40 CFR part 60, appendix B) and must undergo the performance evaluation procedures required by § 63.8 and your site-specific monitoring plan.

If you use a CEMS that uses gas chromatography to measure organic HAP emissions (e.g., carbon disulfide), then that CEMS must be installed, operated, and maintained according to Performance Specification PS-9 (40 CFR part 60, appendix B) and must undergo the performance evaluation procedures required by § 63.8 and your site-specific monitoring plan.

If you modify or replace monitoring equipment or calibration procedures, then you must update your site-specific monitoring plan to address installation location, equipment/specifications, performance evaluation procedures and acceptance criteria (including calibrations), and conduct a performance evaluation of each CMS per the site-specific plan.

checklist: Confirm the facility is a cellulose food casing operation and determine whether the plant is a "major source" of HAP (single HAP ≥ 9.1 Mg/yr (10 tpy) or total HAP ≥ 23 Mg/yr (25 tpy)).

Confirm whether the existing GC/PID instrument is currently used/defined as a CMS/CEMS/CPMS under Subpart UUUU and identify which regulatory monitoring role the instrument serves (process/control outlet, leak detection, parametric monitor, etc.).

Identify whether the Baseline-MOCON Model 8900 will be used as a CEMS/CPMS (continuous emission or parameter monitoring) or only for other purposes; determine whether it is a gas chromatograph (GC) or a different analyzer technology for H2S and CS2.

Determine whether the Baseline-MOCON 8900 meets the applicable Performance Specification(s): PS-7 for H2S CEMS and PS-9 for GC-based organic HAP CEMS (or if it deviates from those PS requirements, document how it differs).

If the Baseline-MOCON 8900 deviates from the applicable PS or the monitoring method specified in the relevant standard, prepare an application for alternative monitoring under § 63.8(f) (include description addressing the four elements in § 63.2 and a performance evaluation test plan per § 63.8(e)(3)); if the instrument will be used as the performance test method, plan to submit at least 60 days before the performance evaluation.

Update or prepare the site-specific monitoring/OM&M plan to document installation location, sample interface, analyzer specs, calibration procedures, performance evaluation procedures and acceptance criteria, QA/QC, and recordkeeping/reporting (per § 63.5545(a) and (b)).

Plan and document the performance evaluation schedule and procedures and be ready to conduct performance evaluations per the site-specific plan and § 63.8 (including notifying the Administrator where required).

Verify CMS cycle time and data reduction requirements applicable to the monitor (e.g., CEMS/CPMS must complete a cycle at least every 15 minutes; valid hourly averages require ≥75% valid hours/data points; follow data averaging and exclusion rules for malfunctions/QA).

Ensure calibration gases and calibration procedures (zero/span/drift checks) required by the applicable performance specification or by the approved alternative method are available and documented in the OM&M plan.

Maintain records of inspections, calibrations, validation checks, performance-evaluation results, and any Administrator approvals for alternative monitoring; be prepared to provide these for inspection and for semiannual/annual reports as required.

candidates.title: General Provisions (Subpart A)

criteria.criterion: If the owner or operator applies in writing and the Administrator determines the source is meeting the relevant standard(s) on a continuous basis or the source is operating under an extension of compliance, then an individual performance test may be waived.

If the owner or operator demonstrates by other means to the Administrator's satisfaction that the affected source is in compliance with the relevant standard, then the Administrator may waive the requirement for the performance test.

If an application for a waiver is submitted, it must include information justifying the waiver (such as technical or economic infeasibility, or impracticality) and, if no site‑specific test plan is submitted, it must be submitted at least 60 days before the performance test.

candidates.title: Performance test methods and procedures (Subpart EE)

criteria.criterion: If multiple emission points are vented to one common control device, then only one performance test is required to demonstrate initial compliance for that group of emission points.

If affected emission points to be tested are located in an area with other gaseous emission sources not affected by this subpart, then during a performance test the owner or operator must isolate the affected emission points either by building a temporary total enclosure or by shutting down all gaseous emission points not affected by the subpart and venting affected emissions through stacks suitable for testing.

If the requirements of §63.7(e)(2)(iv) or §63.7(h) are met (e.g., Administrator waives testing or owner demonstrates compliance by other means), then the owner or operator is not required to conduct an initial performance test under this subpart.

candidates.title: Extension of compliance and waivers (Subpart YY)

criteria.criterion: If the owner or operator applies in writing and the Administrator, in the Administrator's judgment, finds the source is meeting the relevant standard(s) on a continuous basis or is operating under an extension of compliance, then individual performance tests may be waived.

If an application to waive a performance test is submitted it must include information justifying the waiver (such as technical or economic infeasibility or impracticality) and, if no site‑specific test plan is submitted, it must be submitted at least 60 days before the performance test.

candidates.title: Electric arc furnaces and AOD vessels requirements (Subpart YYYYY)

criteria.criterion: If emissions from an EAF or AOD vessel are combined with emissions from facilities not subject to this subpart, then you must notify and receive approval from the Administrator for the procedures that will be used to determine compliance for those emissions.

If you own or operate an affected EAF or AOD subject to a PM performance test, you must conduct the PM performance test according to §63.7 and the listed test methods, except that an existing affected source may certify initial compliance based on a prior performance test conducted within 5 years using the specified methods if that prior test was representative of current conditions.

If emissions from any EAF or AOD are combined with emissions from sources not subject to this subpart, then for melt‑shop opacity you must demonstrate compliance based only on emissions from the sources subject to this subpart.

checklist: Confirm whether the argon stir stations are part of an EAF or AOD affected source subject to Subpart YYYYY.

Confirm whether the argon stir station exhausts are ducted to the same baghouse/control device as emissions from the ladle metallurgical furnace (i.e., whether multiple emission points vent to one common control device).
If emissions are combined, determine whether the other sources vented to the same baghouse are subject to the same NESHAP subpart or are not subject to the subpart (i.e., mixed-source exhaust).
Check whether a prior, representative performance test for the argon stir stations or the shared control device was conducted within the past 5 years and used the specified test methods.

Assess whether you can isolate the argon stir emission points for testing by building a temporary total enclosure or by shutting down other gaseous emission points during the test (feasibility/safety/operational impacts).
Determine available continuous monitoring, historical operating data, or other means to demonstrate continuous compliance that could support a waiver request to the Administrator.

Prepare documentation of the technical impracticality (how emissions from the baghouse/furnace confound measurement) and any economic/operational constraints to include in a written waiver application.

Verify timing requirements and submittal deadlines (e.g., submit waiver application or alternate monitoring/method requests at least 60 days before the scheduled performance test if no site‑specific test plan is being submitted).

If emissions are combined with sources not subject to Subpart YYYYY, be prepared to notify and obtain Administrator approval for the proposed compliance‑determination procedures per 40 CFR 63.10686(d)(4).

If proposing an alternative test method or site‑specific approach, identify whether Method 301 validation, a site‑specific test plan, or other subpart‑specific provisions will be needed and gather supporting data for Administrator review.

candidates.title: NESHAP for Hydrochloric Acid Production

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate an HCl production facility that produces a liquid HCl product at a concentration of 30 weight percent or greater during normal operations and is located at, or is part of, a major source of HAP, then the facility is subject to this subpart.

If you use a caustic scrubber control device and conduct a performance test, then you must establish the minimum recirculating liquid flow rate as the scrubber operating limit and establish minimum and maximum scrubber effluent pH operating limits based on values measured during the performance test.

If you seek to monitor parameters other than those specified for scrubbers, then you may request approval to do so by submitting a monitoring plan to the Administrator under the procedures referenced in this subpart (i.e., § 63.8(f)).

If you use a caustic scrubber or water scrubber to meet the emission limits in Table 1 to this subpart, then you must keep records of daily average scrubber inlet liquid or recirculating liquid flow rate (as appropriate) and daily average scrubber effluent pH to support your compliance demonstration.

If you elect to use a design evaluation in lieu of a performance test for certain HCl storage tanks and transfer operations not routed to a control device, then the design evaluation for a caustic scrubber must address vent stream composition, constituent concentrations, liquid-to-vapor ratio, scrubbing liquid flow rate and concentration, temperature, and reaction kinetics to establish the design exhaust vent concentration level.

candidates.title: NESHAP for Steel Pickling—HCl Process Facilities and Hydrochloric Acid Regeneration Plants

criteria.criterion: If you are subject to this subpart and use a wet scrubber to achieve compliance, then during the performance test you must establish site-specific operating parameter values for the minimum scrubber makeup water flow rate and, for scrubbers that operate with recirculation, the minimum recirculation water flow rate.

If you establish scrubber operating parameters during an emission test under this subpart, then each operating parameter must be monitored continuously and recorded with sufficient frequency to establish a representative average value for that parameter, but no less frequently than once every 15 minutes, and you may conduct multiple performance tests to establish alternative compliant operating parameter values.

If you are demonstrating compliance via performance testing for an emission control device, then you must conduct the initial performance test according to § 63.7 and the conditions specified by the Administrator.

candidates.title: Procedures for Approval of Alternative Means of Emission Limitation

criteria.criterion: If you seek a determination to use an alternative means of emission limitation to the requirements of design, equipment, work practice, or operational standards of this subpart or a subpart referenced by this subpart, then you may request approval and the Administrator will permit use of the alternative means only if, in the Administrator's judgment, it will achieve equivalent reduction in HAP emissions.

If you request permission to use an alternative means of compliance, then you must collect, verify, and submit information showing the alternative achieves equivalent emission reductions and, if not previously tested, submit a proposed test plan and proposed testing/monitoring/recordkeeping/reporting to support the request.

candidates.title: General Provisions

criteria.criterion: If you request an alternative nonopacity emission standard or other alternative means under an applicable subpart, then the Administrator may permit the alternative only if the owner/operator establishes that it will achieve at least equivalent emission reductions and the Administrator provides public notice and opportunity for comment prior to permitting the alternative.

If you request permission to use an alternative nonopacity emission standard, then you must submit proposed test plans or results of testing and monitoring in accordance with § 63.7 and § 63.8 and ensure testing/monitoring are appropriately quality assured and quality controlled.

If you operate an affected source subject to an applicable standard, then at all times (including startup, shutdown, and malfunction) you must operate and maintain the source and associated pollution control and monitoring equipment consistent with safety and good air pollution control practices for minimizing emissions.

checklist: Confirm whether your facility is an HCl production facility that produces liquid HCl product ≥ 30 weight percent during normal operations.
Confirm whether the facility is part of a major source of HAP (potential to emit ≥ 10 t/yr of any single HAP or ≥ 25 t/yr combined HAP).
Determine which NESHAP subpart applies to your operations (NNNNN vs. CCC or other subparts) based on facility type and processes.

Verify whether the Irgafos V-47 unit is a caustic scrubber control device used to control HCl and/or Cl2 emissions from HCl process vents, storage tanks, or transfer operations covered by the applicable subpart.

Check whether you have an existing performance test for the scrubber within the past 5 years and whether the test measured recirculation flow rate and scrubber effluent pH (and scrubbing liquid concentration if relevant); collect test reports and raw data.

If no suitable performance test exists, plan an initial performance test (site-specific test plan per § 63.7(c)(2)) that measures inlet/outlet HCl/Cl2 and records scrubber inlet/recirculating flow and effluent pH (and scrubbing liquid concentration, temperature, liquid-to-vapor ratio, reaction kinetics as needed).

Determine whether the proposed minimum recirculation flow rate (65 gpm) and scrubbing liquid concentration (≥ 2% caustic) were observed during representative performance test runs or can be demonstrated equivalent via testing or engineering/design evaluation.

If you will seek approval to monitor alternative parameters (e.g., scrubbing liquid concentration instead of pH), prepare a monitoring plan and request approval under § 63.8(f) as referenced in 63.9025(b), including rationale why the parameter demonstrates ongoing compliance.

Ensure your CMS and data collection can meet required monitoring frequency and data availability (at least four equally spaced periods per hour, hourly averages, daily averages, and recordkeeping as specified in 63.9025(a) and 63.9035).

Prepare documentation showing equivalence in emissions reduction (test results, engineering analysis, or design evaluation addressing vent composition, liquid-to-vapor ratio, flow rate, concentration, temperature, reaction kinetics) to support an alternative means request under 63.1113.

Be prepared for the Administrator’s review process, which may include public notice and comment and possible conditioning of approval; assemble proposed recordkeeping, reporting, QA/QC, and operational/maintenance requirements to include in the submittal.

Confirm whether the permitting/approval authority for your location (EPA Region or delegated State agency) will be the reviewer and recipient of the monitoring/alternative means submittal (administrative contact for approvals).
