candidates.title: National Emission Standard for Benzene Waste Operations (Bulk Gasoline Terminals) (Subpart R)

criteria.criterion: If a bulk gasoline terminal subject to §63.422(b)(1) uses a thermal oxidation system, then a continuous parameter monitoring system (CPMS) capable of measuring temperature must be installed in the firebox or in the ductwork immediately downstream from the firebox in a position before any substantial heat exchange occurs.

If a bulk gasoline terminal subject to §63.422(b)(1) uses a flare meeting the requirements in §63.11(b), then a heat‑sensing device (e.g., ultraviolet beam sensor or thermocouple) must be installed in proximity to the pilot light to indicate presence of a flame.

If the owner or operator proposes monitoring an alternative operating parameter (other than the listed parameters), then that alternative monitoring will be allowed only upon demonstrating to the Administrator's satisfaction that the alternative parameter demonstrates continuous compliance with the emission standard in §63.422(b) or §60.112b.

If an alternative parameter is approved, then the owner or operator must operate the vapor processing system so as not to exceed or not to go below, as appropriate, the approved alternative operating parameter value (operation outside those values constitutes a violation of the emission standard).

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Gasoline Distribution Bulk Terminals, Bulk Plants, and Pipeline Facilities (Subpart BBBBBB)

criteria.criterion: If a bulk gasoline terminal uses a thermal oxidation system to meet the emission standard, then a CPMS capable of measuring temperature must be installed in the firebox or in the ductwork immediately downstream from the firebox in a position before any substantial heat exchange occurs.

If the owner/operator elects the alternative for a thermal oxidation system to monitor the pilot flame, then the presence of the pilot flame shall be monitored using a heat‑sensing device (e.g., ultraviolet beam sensor or thermocouple) that sends a positive parameter value when the pilot is on and a negative value when off, and the thermal oxidation system must be equipped to automatically prevent gasoline loading operations when the pilot flame is absent.

If the owner or operator seeks to monitor an alternative operating parameter other than those listed, then the alternative will be allowed upon demonstrating to the Administrator that the alternative parameter demonstrates continuous compliance with the emission standard in §63.11088(a), and the rationale and supporting data must be provided for Administrator approval.

If a flare meeting the requirements in §63.11(b) is used at a bulk gasoline terminal subject to this subpart, then a heat‑sensing device (e.g., ultraviolet beam sensor or thermocouple) must be installed in proximity to the pilot light to indicate presence of a flame.

candidates.title: General Provisions for Control Devices and Work Practices (Subpart A)

criteria.criterion: If owners or operators use flares to comply with applicable subparts, then flares shall be operated at all times when emissions may be vented to them.

If a flare is used, then the presence of the flare pilot flame shall be monitored using a thermocouple or any other equivalent device to detect the presence of a flame and flares shall be operated with a flame present at all times.

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Organic Hazardous Air Pollutants for Equipment Leaks and Process Vents (Subpart G)

criteria.criterion: If a process vent uses an incinerator (non‑catalytic), then a temperature monitoring device equipped with a continuous recorder must be installed in the firebox or in the ductwork immediately downstream of the firebox before any substantial heat exchange occurs.

If a process vent uses a flare, then a device (including but not limited to a thermocouple, ultraviolet beam sensor, or infrared sensor) capable of continuously detecting the presence of a pilot flame is required.

If the owner or operator uses an approved control device but seeks to monitor a parameter other than those specified, then the owner or operator must request approval to monitor alternative parameters according to the procedures specified in this subpart.

checklist: Confirm which EPA gasoline distribution standard the facility is subject to (e.g., whether the terminal is subject to §63.422(b)(1) and Subpart R or to the emission standard in Table 2/item 1(b) of Subpart BBBBBB) and the applicable compliance dates.
Identify the vapor control device type(s) for the affected loading racks (thermal oxidizer/thermal oxidation system (incinerator), flare, carbon adsorber, refrigerated condenser, etc.).

For a thermal oxidizer: verify whether a CPMS temperature sensor is installed in the firebox or in ductwork immediately downstream of the firebox in a position before substantial heat exchange and whether temperature was recorded during the most recent performance test.

For choosing pilot flame monitoring instead of temperature: verify that a heat‑sensing device (ultraviolet beam sensor, thermocouple, infrared sensor, etc.) can be installed in proximity to the pilot, can provide positive/negative parameter output, and meets signal reliability requirements.

Verify whether the vapor control system can automatically prevent gasoline loading operations when the pilot flame is absent (interlock/alarm/shutdown capability) as required by some subpart provisions for pilot‑based monitoring.

Determine whether the flare meets the §63.11(b) design/operation requirements (operated at all times when emissions may be vented to it, operated with a flame present, tip/heat content/velocity as applicable) and whether pilot monitoring via thermocouple is acceptable under the applicable subpart.

Assemble performance test data, engineering analyses, and manufacturer's recommendations to demonstrate that pilot flame monitoring (or any alternative parameter) will show continuous compliance with the applicable emission standard (prepare rationale, data, calculations, and proposed operating parameter value and monitoring frequency for Administrator review).

Confirm how the facility's loading operations (intermittent loading, periods between cargo tanks, known previous contents, and times when vapors are not being displaced) will affect valid operating data and the establishment of operating parameter values and exclusions.

Check facility permits or state/local rules for any enforceable monitoring requirements or operating limits (e.g., limits expressed as mg/L of gasoline loaded or permit‑specified monitored parameters) that may affect eligibility for an alternative monitoring method.

Verify ability to meet continuous monitoring quality assurance: instrument calibration, maintenance, data logging/recordkeeping, and the monitoring and inspection plan elements required by the applicable subpart.

Confirm locations available for temperature sensor vs pilot sensor installation (firebox or duct before heat exchange for temperature; proximity to pilot for flame sensor) and whether installation will conflict with safety or equipment constraints.

candidates.title: Monitoring requirements (steel pickling facilities and acid regeneration plants - Subpart CCC)

criteria.criterion: If the owner or operator is a new, reconstructed, or existing steel pickling facility or acid regeneration plant subject to this subpart, then they are subject to the monitoring requirements including performance tests to measure HCl mass flows at the control device inlet and outlet on the schedule specified or an alternative schedule approved by the permitting authority.

If a wet scrubber is used as the emission control device, then the owner or operator must install, operate, and maintain systems to measure and record scrubber makeup water flow rate and, if required, recirculation water flow rate (monitored continuously and recorded at least once per shift) and must initiate corrective action for excursions below minimum values established during performance testing.

If the owner or operator wishes to implement monitoring different from the requirements of this subpart, then they may develop and implement alternative monitoring requirements only with approval by the Administrator.

candidates.title: Monitoring installation, operation, and maintenance requirements (Subpart NNNNN)

criteria.criterion: If you are required by § 63.9020(e) to monitor an operating parameter, then you must install, operate, and maintain each continuous monitoring system according to the CMS requirements (operate CMS whenever process is operating, collect data from at least four equally spaced periods each hour, have valid data for at least 75 percent of operating hours, calculate hourly and daily averages, and record inspections/calibrations per site-specific monitoring plan).

If you use a scrubber control device and wish to monitor parameters other than those specified in § 63.9020(e), then you may request approval under § 63.8(f) by submitting a monitoring plan that (a) identifies the operating parameter to ensure control efficiency is maintained, (b) discusses why the parameter is appropriate, and (c) identifies the specific monitoring procedures.

If you request to monitor alternative parameters, then your request must include a description of affected sources and parameters, methods to demonstrate suitability and a schedule, certification that you will establish an operating limit representing conditions during the control device performance test, frequency and content of monitoring/recording/reporting (if not continuous), supporting calculations, and the averaging time.

candidates.title: General monitoring requirements for control and recovery devices (Subpart SS)

criteria.criterion: If you are the owner or operator of a regulated source required to monitor under this subpart, then monitoring shall be conducted as set forth in this section and relevant subpart sections unless the Administrator approves alternatives.

If you wish to use alternatives to the continuous operating parameter monitoring and recordkeeping provisions or to monitor a different parameter than those listed, then you may request approval to do so as specified in paragraph (d) of this section.

If a CPMS is used, then it must be installed, calibrated, maintained, and operated according to manufacturer's specifications or other written procedures that provide adequate assurance of accurate monitoring and must be repaired or replaced promptly for routine malfunctions.

candidates.title: What are my monitoring alternatives? (Subpart UUU)

criteria.criterion: If you use an add-on control device not listed in the subpart or wish to monitor an alternative parameter, then you must request approval to monitor alternative parameters by submitting a request for review and approval to the Administrator that includes the required descriptions and justifications.

If you request approval to monitor alternative parameters, then your submission must include a description of each affected source and the parameter(s), a description of methods and procedures to demonstrate the parameter's suitability and schedule, certification that you will establish an operating limit representing compliant conditions, the proposed frequency/content of monitoring/recording/reporting if not continuous (with rationale), supporting calculations, and the averaging time.

checklist: Determine whether your facility is a steel pickling facility or an acid regeneration plant that is subject to Subpart CCC (40 CFR 63.1162).
Confirm the type of HCl control device in use (are the HCl bubblers characterized/treated as a wet scrubber/absorber or a different control device under the applicable subpart?).

Collect and have available the most recent performance test results that establish HCl control efficiency and any minimum operating values (e.g., flow rates, immersion depths) used to set operating limits during the performance test (per 40 CFR 63.1162(a)(1) and 63.1162(a)(2)).

Document current monitoring practice: which parameters are monitored, monitoring frequencies, data collection intervals, averaging methods, and whether CMS meet requirements of four equally spaced periods per hour and 75% valid-data rules if applicable (40 CFR 63.9025(a)(1)-(5)).
Verify monitoring equipment certification and calibration schedules (manufacturer accuracy within 5% and calibration at least annually) where required (40 CFR 63.1162(a)(5); 40 CFR 63.1162(b)(3)).

Demonstrate how proposed alternative parameters (e.g., minimum dipleg immersion depth, maximum time between liquid change-outs) correlate to control efficiency established during the initial performance test and prepare supporting calculations and rationale (per 40 CFR 63.9025(b)(1)-(3) and 63.1573(f)).

Prepare a monitoring plan or request for alternative monitoring that includes: identification of the parameter(s) to be monitored, justification why the parameter demonstrates ongoing compliance, specific monitoring procedures, frequency/averaging/recording details, QA/QC/performance specifications, supporting calculations, and proposed operating limits tied to performance test conditions (40 CFR 63.9025(b)(1)-(3); 40 CFR 63.9025(f)(1)-(5); 40 CFR 63.1573(f)(1)-(5)).

Confirm the proposed data recording and reporting scheme meets the applicable CMS requirements (e.g., hourly/daily averages, records of inspections/calibrations) or explicitly state when monitoring will be non-continuous and provide rationale (40 CFR 63.9025(a)(4)-(6); 40 CFR 63.9025(f)(3)).

Check whether any existing permit (e.g., Title V) or prior Administrator/permitting authority approvals restrict alternative monitoring, and be prepared to submit the alternative monitoring request per § 63.8(f) to the Administrator and permitting authority.

If your control device is covered under another referenced subpart's mandatory operating limits (e.g., establishment of limits during performance tests), confirm that any proposed alternative monitoring will establish operating limits that reflect the conditions when the control device met the standard (see requirements to establish levels during performance testing in relevant subparts).

Those criteria capture EPA’s conditional approval pending a successful performance test."}

candidates.title: Control device and work practice requirements (General Provisions)

criteria.criterion: If an individual NESHAP subpart references §63.11, then the control device and alternative work practice requirements in §63.11 apply to sources subject to that subpart.

If the applicable subpart requires monitoring of equipment with a 40 CFR part 60, appendix A-7, Method 21 monitor, then you may instead use the alternative optical gas imaging work practice described in §63.11(c)–(e).

candidates.title: Monitoring and demonstrating continuous compliance (Subpart VVVV)

criteria.criterion: If you have an emission capture system enclosure that vents to an add-on control device, then you must install and record either a flow-rate device or a duct static pressure device for the duct from each enclosure to the add-on control device.

If a capture device is not part of a permanent total enclosure, then you must establish operating limits for either gas volumetric flow rate or duct static pressure and an operating limit for pressure drop across at least one opening in each enclosure (operating limits for PTEs are specified elsewhere in the subpart).

If you propose an alternative monitoring approach for a control device not listed in the subpart, then you must obtain Administrator approval of site-specific alternative monitoring requirements under §63.8(f) and submit the monitoring plan for approval prior to using the alternative.

candidates.title: Monitoring requirements and capture/collection verification (Subpart RRR)

criteria.criterion: If you install and operate a capture/collection system for an affected source with an add-on control device, then you must inspect annually and either (a) perform an annual volumetric flow measurement using Methods 1 and 2 or verify a permanent total enclosure using Method 204, or (b) follow one of the specified alternate procedures (including static pressure downstream of the hood) to maintain operations consistent with the performance test operating limit.

If you choose the alternate procedure that uses a duct static pressure device immediately downstream of the hood exit, then you must take daily pressure readings (three measurements separated by ≥5 minutes, averaged) and maintain those daily averages at or above 90 percent of the average vacuum recorded during the most recent Method 2 performance test series.

If you choose to verify a permanent total enclosure by continuous negative-pressure monitoring as an alternative to Method 204, then you must install a representative pressure indicator, record pressure daily (or interlock to halt feed if negative pressure is lost), and inspect the indicator at least annually.

candidates.title: Monitoring requirements and alternate monitoring approval (Subpart LLL)

criteria.criterion: If you wish to use an alternate monitoring requirement to demonstrate compliance with this subpart, then you must submit an application to the Administrator containing data justifying the request, a description of the proposed alternative monitoring approach, and data showing the alternative provides equivalent or better assurance of compliance.

If a conveying transfer point is a permanent total (totally enclosed) conveying system, then that transfer point is not required to conduct Method 22 visible emissions monitoring and must be operated and maintained as a total enclosure per the facility operations and maintenance plan.

checklist: Identify which NESHAP subpart(s) actually apply to each of your ten emission units (determine whether the units fall under the subparts cited above).

Confirm whether each enclosure feeding the RTO is a Permanent Total Enclosure (PTE) verified by EPA Method 204 and provide date and results of the most recent Method 204 verification (or Method 1/2 performance test if used).

Obtain the numerical results from the most recent Method 1/2 performance test(s): average duct flow, average duct static pressure (vacuum), and the datum values used to set operating limits during the performance test.

Document whether the duct between the enclosure(s) and the RTO has an installed static pressure sensor (location and distance from hood/enclosure and control device) and whether the sensor meets siting requirements to provide a representative duct static pressure measurement.

If proposing daily static-pressure-based monitoring: record the procedure you will use (three readings ≥5 minutes apart, averaging method), and calculate the 90% threshold (90% of the Method 2 average vacuum) you will maintain.

Verify whether any bypass lines exist that could divert flow away from the RTO and document how bypass valves are secured or monitored (e.g., position indicator, car-seal, continuous monitoring, or automatic shutdown).

Confirm RTO is the add-on control device for the enclosures and document any other control devices, their monitoring requirements, and whether the proposal would affect monitoring at the control device inlet.

Prepare test data, engineering rationale, and supporting calculations showing that duct static pressure to the RTO is an appropriate surrogate for facial velocity/natural-draft opening monitoring and that it will provide equivalent or better assurance of capture efficiency (to include sensor siting, averaging time, QA/QC, calibration frequency).

Assemble a written monitoring plan that follows the applicable subpart requirements (site-specific operating limits, monitoring frequency, O&M and QA/QC procedures) to submit to the Administrator (or permitting authority) for approval before implementing the alternative.

Confirm daily operational procedures: pressure-tap check frequency, calibrations (quarterly/ monthly as required), recordkeeping retention, and automatic waste-feed or process interlocks if pressure falls below allowable limits.

If applying for alternative monitoring approval, note the required timing and content for the application per the applicable subpart (e.g., submit with notification of performance test or comprehensive performance test plan) and the Administrator's response timelines.
Retain records of all monitoring, inspections, calibrations, and any deviations; verify the recordkeeping and reporting periods required by the applicable subpart(s).

These criteria capture the EPA note that the alternative static-pressure method was approved for demonstrating continuous compliance with PTE requirements."}

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants From Natural Gas Processing Plants (Subpart HH)

criteria.criterion: If ancillary equipment or compressors are located at a natural gas processing plant and operate in VHAP service equal to or greater than 300 hours per calendar year, then they are subject to the equipment leak standards in this subpart.

If an owner or operator demonstrates that the percent VHAP content of the process fluid in a piece of ancillary equipment or compressor can be reasonably expected never to exceed 10.0 percent by weight, then that piece of equipment is not considered to be in VHAP service for purposes of this subpart.
If the ancillary equipment or compressors are subject to and controlled under the requirements of subpart H of this part or 40 CFR part 60, subpart OOOO, then § 63.769 does not apply to them.

If the plant is a nonfractionating plant that does not have the design capacity to process 283,000 standard cubic meters per day or more of field gas, then pumps in VHAP service, valves in gas/vapor and light liquid service, and pressure relief devices in gas/vapor service located at that plant are exempt from the routine monitoring requirements and from paragraphs (c)(1) through (3) of § 63.769.

If a pressure relief device is in gas/vapor service, then it must be monitored quarterly and within 5 days after each pressure release to detect leaks, a leak is detected at an instrument reading of 10,000 ppm or greater, and detected leaks must be repaired as soon as practicable but no later than 15 calendar days (unless delayed under the referenced provisions).

candidates.title: General Provisions (Alternative Work Practice for Leak Monitoring) (Subpart A)

criteria.criterion: If an applicable subpart requires monitoring of equipment with a 40 CFR part 60, appendix A-7, Method 21 monitor, then the owner or operator may elect to use the alternative work practice (optical gas imaging) instead of Method 21, subject to the requirements in § 63.11(c)–(e).

If the alternative work practice is used to identify leaks, then the owner or operator must document the equipment/process units for which the alternative work practice will be used and must follow the instrument specifications, daily instrument check, leak survey procedures, and recordkeeping/reporting requirements in § 63.11(e).

If the alternative work practice is chosen, then the owner or operator must (1) choose one of the monitoring frequencies listed in Table 1 to subpart A in lieu of the applicable subpart's Method 21 frequency, and (2) conduct annual Method 21 screening of the regulated equipment monitored by the alternative work practice and keep the Method 21 results as required.

If the alternative work practice is used and a leak is detected by imaging or visual evidence (e.g., liquid dripping), then the leak must be identified for repair and re-screening after an attempted repair must be done either by the alternative work practice or Method 21 at the leak definition in the applicable subpart.

candidates.title: Test Methods and Procedures (Method 21 performance and calibration requirements) (Subpart H)

criteria.criterion: If monitoring is required under the referencing subpart using Method 21, then monitoring shall comply with Method 21 of 40 CFR part 60, appendix A, including the Method 21 instrument performance criteria, daily calibration before use, and specified calibration gases.

If an owner or operator elects to adjust instrument readings for background when using Method 21, then they must determine and use the background level per the procedures in § 63.180(c) and compare the arithmetic difference to the applicable leak definition.

If an owner or operator wishes to demonstrate that a piece of equipment is not in organic HAP service for purposes of Method 21 applicability, then the piece is presumed to be in organic HAP service unless the owner demonstrates the percent organic HAP content does not exceed 5 percent by weight using Method 18 (or ASTM where allowed) as specified in § 63.180(d).

candidates.title: Instrument and Sensory Monitoring for Leaks (Subpart TT)

criteria.criterion: If a regulated source is subject to Subpart TT, then instrument monitoring for leaks shall comply with Method 21 of 40 CFR part 60, appendix A (monitoring method), the Method 21 performance criteria, daily calibration, and calibration gas specifications set out in § 63.1004(b).

If an owner or operator elects to adjust or not to adjust instrument readings for background under Subpart TT, then the procedures of § 63.1004(c) apply (follow Method 21 background determination and compare arithmetic difference to the applicable leak definitions).

If monitoring under Subpart TT is performed, then monitoring shall be performed when the equipment is in regulated material service or in use with any other detectable material as required in § 63.1004(b)(5).

checklist: Confirm whether your facility is a 'natural gas processing plant' as defined in 40 CFR 63.761.

For each piece of ancillary equipment and each compressor, determine the VHAP concentration (percent by weight) of the fluid it contains or contacts using the procedures in 40 CFR 63.772(a) (e.g., Method 18 or ASTM D6420) to decide if it is 'in VHAP service' (≥ 10% VHAP) or not.
For each ancillary item found to be in VHAP service, record the number of hours it operates in VHAP service per calendar year to check the ≥ 300 hours/year applicability threshold in § 63.769(a).
Determine whether any ancillary equipment or compressors are already subject to and controlled under 40 CFR part 63 subpart H or 40 CFR part 60 subpart OOOO (if so, § 63.769(b) may not apply).

Determine whether the plant is a nonfractionating facility and whether it has design capacity to process ≥ 283,000 standard cubic meters per day of field gas (to establish applicability of the exemption in § 63.769(c)(5)).

Identify which pieces are pumps, valves (gas/vapor or light liquid), and pressure relief devices and whether they are in gas/vapor or light liquid service (since § 63.769(c)(5) and (c)(1) address those categories specifically).

If you propose to replace Method 21 with another approach, decide whether you will use the Subpart A alternative work practice (optical gas imaging) or some other approved method; note that Subpart A AWP requires OGI (not just naked-eye visual inspection) and has instrument specs, daily checks, and annual Method 21 screening requirements (review § 63.11(e) and § 63.11(d)(7)).

If using Subpart A AWP (OGI), verify you can meet the OGI instrument requirements: provide image at detection sensitivity and distance, daily instrument check using the specified mass flow calculation and video/time-stamp records, and retain video and daily-check records for 5 years (§ 63.11(e)(1)–(2), (e)(4)–(5)).

If you intend to use Method 21, verify you have a Method 21-capable instrument that meets the performance criteria, can be calibrated daily with required calibration gases (zero air and methane-in-air as specified), and you can perform background adjustments per the cited procedures (§ 63.180 and § 63.1004).

Decide and document the monitoring frequency: if you use the Subpart A alternative work practice you must choose a frequency from Table 1 to subpart A (see § 63.11(d)(5)); otherwise follow the frequency specified in the applicable subpart (e.g., § 63.769(c)(1) for PRDs requires quarterly monitoring).
Prepare to keep required records for inspections, leaks, repairs, instrument IDs, dates/times, and Method 21 annual screenings as required by § 63.774 and § 63.11(e)(4)–(5).

If you detect a leak (by any chosen detection method), be prepared to follow the repair timing and documentation requirements (first attempt ≤5 days, repair completed ≤15 days unless permitted to delay) as specified in the applicable provisions (e.g., § 63.769(c)(3), § 63.773(c)(3)).

candidates.title: General Provisions

criteria.criterion: If the owner or operator intends to conduct a performance test, then the owner or operator must notify the Administrator in writing of the intention at least 60 calendar days before the performance test is initially scheduled to begin.

If a force majeure is about to occur, occurs, or has occurred and the owner or operator intends to assert a claim of force majeure for delay in testing beyond the regulatory deadline, then the owner or operator must notify the Administrator in writing as soon as practicable, provide a description and rationale, propose a new test date, and the Administrator may grant an extension at their sole discretion.

If the owner or operator requests a waiver of an initial or subsequent performance test, then the application for a waiver must be submitted at least 60 days before the performance test if the site-specific test plan is not submitted (or as otherwise specified for waiver accompanying extension requests).

If the owner or operator wishes to change an applicable time period or postmark deadline (including scheduling), then the owner or operator may request an adjustment in writing as soon as practicable and the Administrator will notify approval or disapproval within 15 calendar days after receiving sufficient information to evaluate the request.

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Asphalt Roofing Manufacturing (Subpart LLLLL)

criteria.criterion: If you are required to conduct a performance test under this subpart, then you must submit a notification of intent to conduct a performance test at least 60 calendar days before the performance test is scheduled to begin.

If you elect to use results of a previously-conducted emission test to demonstrate initial compliance, then you must submit the prior test data in lieu of initial performance test results with the Notification of Compliance Status and demonstrate the prior-test conditions meet the subpart's requirements.

If you are required to submit a Notification of Compliance Status after conducting a performance test, then you must submit that Notification of Compliance Status, including the performance test results, before the close of business on the 60th calendar day following completion of the performance test.

candidates.title: Notification, Recordkeeping, and Reporting Requirements (Subpart AAAAAAA)

criteria.criterion: If you are subject to this subpart and required to conduct a compliance test, then you must submit a notification of intent to conduct the compliance test at least 60 calendar days before the compliance test is scheduled to begin.

If you are using data from a previously-conducted emission test to serve as documentation of compliance, then you must submit those test data in lieu of the initial compliance test results with the Notification of Compliance Status.

checklist: Confirm which NESHAP subpart(s) applies to your facility (e.g., Subpart LLLLL for asphalt roofing) and whether any State (Oregon) has been delegated authority so notifications go to EPA Regional Office or State (see 40 CFR 63.9(a)(4)).
Determine whether your affected source is new or existing, and the applicable compliance and initial performance-test deadlines (see 40 CFR 63.8686(a) for 180‑day timing).

Decide whether you will use a previously-conducted emission test to avoid an on-site initial performance test and verify that the prior test meets the subpart criteria (no process changes, within the last 60 months/5 years, matching operating conditions and methods) per 40 CFR 63.8686(b) and 63.8692(f)/63.11564(a)(6).

Verify whether a site-specific test plan will be submitted and whether the Administrator has requested review (if no site-specific plan is submitted, waiver application timing rules apply) per 40 CFR 63.7(c) and 63.7(h)(3).

If planning to test during your highest production period and that conflicts with the 60‑day notification, decide whether you will (a) request an adjustment to time periods or postmark deadlines under 40 CFR 63.9(i), (b) apply for a waiver of the performance test under 40 CFR 63.7(h), or (c) assert force majeure under 40 CFR 63.7(a)(4); prepare the written justification and supporting information required for the chosen route.

Prepare the written notification or request early (include proposed test dates, site‑specific test plan if requested, justification for waiver or adjustment, and any force majeure description) and be ready to provide any additional information the Administrator requests.

Confirm where to submit notifications and reports (EPA Regional Office vs delegated State authority) and whether you must submit electronically via CEDRI/CDX (see 40 CFR 63.9(a)(4) and subpart-specific reporting provisions).

If using alternative test methods or needing audit samples, confirm the 60‑day notification obligations for alternative-method validation and the Method 301 requirements per 40 CFR 63.7(f) and 63.7(c)(2)(i).
Keep records to demonstrate representative 'normal operating conditions' during the test and retention of test records for at least 5 years as required by 40 CFR 63.7(g)(3).

candidates.title: General Provisions

criteria.criterion: If an owner or operator wishes to use an alternative monitoring procedure, then they must submit an application to the Administrator that describes the proposed alternative (addressing the four elements of monitoring) and includes a performance evaluation test plan if required.

If the alternative monitoring procedure will serve as the performance test method, then the application must be submitted at least 60 days before the performance evaluation is scheduled to begin and must meet the alternative test method requirements under §63.7(f).

If the Administrator approves the use of an alternative monitoring method, then the owner or operator shall continue to use the approved alternative method until the Administrator approves another monitoring method.

If installation or use of a CMS specified by a relevant standard would not provide accurate measurements due to interferences (e.g., liquid water or other effluents), then the Administrator may approve alternative monitoring requirements or procedures.

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Chromium Electroplating and Anodizing (Subpart N)

criteria.criterion: If an owner or operator subject to this subpart wishes to request and obtain approval for an alternative monitoring method, then the request and approval shall be considered in accordance with the procedures in §63.8(f)(1), (f)(3), (f)(4), and (f)(5).

If an owner or operator uses an air pollution control device not listed in this subpart, then the owner/operator must submit a description of the device, performance test results collected per §63.344(c), a copy of the operation and maintenance plan (including practices), and proposed operating parameters to be monitored for continuous compliance; the monitoring plan is subject to Administrator approval.

If installation or use of monitoring devices specified in this subpart would not provide accurate measurements due to interferences or if alternate monitoring locations would provide representative measurements, then the Administrator may approve alternative monitoring methods under this subpart.

candidates.title: Alternative Compliance Application Example (Subpart QQQQQ)

criteria.criterion: If a source uses a control technique other than a solvent recovery system and/or solvent substitution, then the owner/operator may request approval to use an alternative method of demonstrating compliance by submitting a description of the proposed testing, monitoring, recordkeeping, and reporting and the proposed basis for demonstrating compliance.

If the alternative demonstration request is based on previously performed testing, then the owner/operator must submit the testing results, a description of the procedures followed, and the pertinent conditions during testing; if no prior testing, the owner/operator must submit a proposed test plan.
If an alternative method of demonstrating compliance is proposed, then use of the alternative method must not begin until approval is granted by the Administrator.

candidates.title: Alternative Monitoring for Continuous Emissions Monitoring Systems (Subpart EEEEE)

criteria.criterion: If a source requests an alternative monitoring method for a continuous emissions monitoring system, then the owner/operator must submit a monitoring plan describing the control technique or prevention technique, the continuous monitoring system or method (including operating parameters), test results demonstrating compliance, operating limit(s) (if applicable), and the frequency of measurement and recording to establish continuous compliance.

If a monitoring plan for an alternative monitoring method is submitted, then the monitoring plan is subject to approval by the Administrator and use of the alternative monitoring method must not begin until approval is granted.

checklist: Confirm each tank is an enclosed hard chromium electroplating tank (count: 3) and whether each tank is a new, existing, or reconstructed affected source.

Determine whether the facility is classified as a large or small hard chromium electroplating facility by calculating maximum cumulative potential and actual cumulative rectifier capacity (12-month rolling), and prepare to maintain monthly ampere-hour records as required.

Identify the control device(s) to be used (Palm Technology Emission Eliminating Devices) and verify whether that device is specifically listed in §63.342 Table 1 or otherwise covered by the subpart; if not listed, prepare the device description and test data required by 63.343(d).

Assess feasibility of required standard monitoring and test methods for your equipment: Method 306/306A sampling (120 min, 1.70 dscm per run), Method 306B surface tension measurements, pressure-drop and velocity-pressure monitoring locations and instrumentation, and sampling port access for Method 306.

Document specific reasons the standard monitoring methods are not feasible for your equipment (e.g., inability to install sampling ports, liquid water or effluent interferences, access constraints) to justify an alternative monitoring request.

Decide whether the proposed alternative monitoring will be used as the performance test method; if yes, plan to submit the application at least 60 days before the performance evaluation and include Method 301 validation if replacing a test method per §63.7(f).

Prepare a monitoring application/plan that: (a) describes the alternative monitoring system addressing the four elements of monitoring (per §63.2), (b) includes a site-specific performance evaluation/test plan (per §63.8(e)(3) and §63.7(c)), (c) provides QA/QC and performance evaluation details, and (d) justifies technical impracticability of specified methods.

Assess whether the requested change is a minor, intermediate, or major change (definitions in §63.90) because major alternatives to monitoring require Administrator approval and may not be delegable to State authorities (see §63.348(c)(3)).

Assemble test data or plans to demonstrate performance of the Palm Technology devices (Method 306/306A runs or validated alternative) and identify the operating parameter(s) proposed for continuous compliance monitoring (e.g., pressure drop, mass emission calculation, alternative parameter).

Plan to include operation and maintenance plan elements required by §63.342(f)(3) (O&M criteria, checklist, procedures for malfunctions and corrective actions, housekeeping practices) and to submit or incorporate those into the monitoring/approval package.

Prepare to retain and provide, upon request, all records of the site-specific performance evaluation or performance test report (including raw data, QA, and calculations) and to comply with reporting timelines for notification and performance test results.

If seeking approval from a delegated State agency, verify whether the approval authority for the specific alternative (especially major alternatives) is retained by the EPA Administrator per §63.348(c)(3) and, if so, plan to submit the request to the appropriate EPA Regional Office.

Thus the key reasons in the EPA notes are captured."}

candidates.title: Chemical Manufacturing Process Units (heat exchange system requirements)

criteria.criterion: If the plant operates a heat exchange system used to cool process equipment in a chemical manufacturing process unit that meets the applicability criteria in §63.100(b)(1)–(3) and is not excluded by any paragraph of §63.104(a), then the heat exchange system must be monitored under §63.104 according to paragraphs (b) or (c) (or other applicable paragraphs).

If the owner/operator elects to monitor the cooling water for organic HAPs under §63.104(b), then cooling-water concentrations must be determined using any EPA-approved method listed in 40 CFR part 136 that is sensitive to concentrations as low as 10 parts per million and the same analytical method must be used for both entrance and exit samples, unless an alternative method is approved by the Administrator.

If monitoring under §63.104(b), then samples must be collected at the entrance and exit points defined in §63.104(b)(4) and a minimum of three sets of samples must be taken at each entrance and exit with the entrance and exit averages calculated and corrected for makeup water or evaporation as applicable.

If monitoring under §63.104(b), then monitoring frequency must be monthly for the first 6 months and quarterly thereafter (unless other paragraphs change frequency), and a leak is detected using the statistical test in §63.104(b)(6) (one-sided at α=0.05 and ≥1 ppm or 10 percent of entrance mean, whichever is greater).

If the owner/operator elects to use surrogate indicators instead of direct cooling-water HAP analysis under §63.104(c), then the owner/operator must prepare and implement a written monitoring plan describing the surrogate(s), how they indicate leaks, the parameter levels that constitute a leak (documented with data/calculations), monitoring frequency (no less than monthly first 6 months and quarterly thereafter), and recordkeeping, and must revise the plan within 180 days if the surrogate fails to identify a substantial leak discovered by other means.

If an analytical or sampling approach different from that specified in §63.104(b) is proposed for cooling-water monitoring (e.g., composite vs. grab), then the approach must either be an EPA-approved part 136 method that meets the sensitivity and sampling-location/number requirements of §63.104(b) or be approved as an alternative method by the Administrator.

candidates.title: Process Vents, Transfer Operations, and Wastewater (sampling and test method provisions)

criteria.criterion: If conducting process-vent or control-device performance testing under Subpart G methods (e.g., Method 18, Method 25A, Method 320, or other methods validated per Method 301), then minimum sampling times and allowable sample types are specified and either an integrated (composite) sample or multiple grab samples may be used where the cited method allows it.

If performing a Method 18 or Method 25A run for vent or control-device testing as specified in Subpart G, then the minimum sampling time for each run is 1 hour and the run may consist of either an integrated sample or four grab samples taken at approximately equal time intervals (e.g., 15-minute intervals).

If conducting wastewater performance tests under §63.145 for concentration or percent removal/destruction options, then samples may be grab samples or composite samples, taken at approximately equally spaced intervals over a 1-hour period, and each performance-test run must consist of a minimum of 3 runs.

If proposing use of a test or sampling method other than the specified Method 18/25A/320/part-136 methods, then the alternative method or data must be validated according to the protocol in Method 301 of appendix A (or be approved by the Administrator) before it may be used to demonstrate compliance.

If you seek to monitor parameters other than those listed for process vents or recovery devices in §63.114(a)–(b), then you must request approval to do so under the procedures specified in §63.114(c) (i.e., submit the request per §63.151(f) or §63.152(e) of this subpart as referenced).

checklist: Confirm the source is a chemical manufacturing process unit subject to subpart F criteria in 40 CFR 63.100(b)(1)–(3) (i.e., primary product list and Table 2 HAP usage and plant is a major source).

Determine whether the heat exchange system is in organic HAP service or in ethylene oxide service (check process-fluid composition, % HAP and % ethylene oxide) per 40 CFR 63.101 and §63.109 so that the correct subpart-F requirements apply.
Decide which monitoring route you will elect under §63.104: (b) direct cooling-water monitoring, (c) surrogate indicator monitoring, (g)/(l) or other; and document that election.

For cooling-water monitoring under §63.104(b): identify entrance and exit sampling locations as defined in §63.104(b)(4), plan for a minimum of three sets of entrance/exit samples per monitoring event, and set monitoring frequency (monthly first 6 months, then quarterly) per §63.104(b)(1) and (5).

Verify the analytical method you plan to use is an EPA-approved part 136 method sensitive to 10 ppm (or better) and that the same method will be used for entrance and exit; if your proposed composite sampling approach is part of a given method, confirm that method explicitly permits composite/integrated sampling (or allows it via Method 301 validation).

If your proposed composite sampling is not explicitly allowed by the cited part-136 method, prepare a Method 301 validation package or an alternative-method approval request to the Administrator showing equivalence (see 40 CFR 63.115(c)(2), 63.128(a)(11), 63.145(i)(4)).

If you propose an alternative monitoring parameter (not one of the parameters listed in §63.114(a)/(b)), prepare and submit a parameter-change/alternative monitoring approval request per 40 CFR 63.114(c) and the referenced submission procedures (§63.151(f) or §63.152(e)).

Confirm whether Louisiana is the delegated permitting authority for Part 63 in your area or whether approval must be sought from EPA Region (determine whether Administrator approval is required or the state can approve alternative methods/monitoring plans).

If electing surrogate monitoring under §63.104(c), prepare the written monitoring plan that documents the surrogate(s), demonstration data/calculations for leak thresholds, monitoring frequency, recordkeeping, and procedures for plan revision if a leak is missed.

Verify sample handling/holding requirements for the chosen method (e.g., preservation, storage, analysis timeframe) and ensure your field sampling protocol minimizes loss and preserves sample integrity (Subpart G/§63.145 sampling-plan and Method 301 validation requirements).

Document how you will perform the statistical leak test (entrance vs exit means) described in §63.104(b)(6) and plan actions (repair timing, delay-of-repair/justification, re-monitoring and reporting) in accordance with §63.104(d)–(f).

candidates.title: General Provisions

criteria.criterion: If the owner or operator of an existing source is unable to comply with a relevant standard established under this part pursuant to section 112(d) and additional time is necessary for installation of controls, then the owner or operator may request that the Administrator (or an approved State authority) grant up to 1 additional year to comply.

If an owner or operator requests an extension under paragraph (i)(4), then the request must be submitted in writing no later than 120 days prior to the affected source's compliance date, except that a request may be submitted after that date if the need for the extension arose after that date due to circumstances beyond the owner's reasonable control and the request includes a statement of the reasons and the date when the owner first learned of the problems.

If requesting an extension under paragraph (i)(4), then the request must include a description of the controls to be installed and a compliance schedule that at minimum lists the dates by which on-site construction or installation will be initiated and the date by which final compliance will be achieved (and may include interim steps and controls as specified).

candidates.title: Primary Aluminum Production

criteria.criterion: If an owner or operator of an existing facility is subject to Subpart LL, then the compliance date for the pitch storage tank POM limit provisions was October 16, 2017.

If an existing pitch storage tank was shut down at the time compliance would have otherwise been required and is subsequently restarted, then the owner or operator must conduct the initial performance test by the 30th day following startup.

If the owner or operator demonstrates initial compliance for a pitch storage tank by performance testing, then the control efficiency for POM during tank loading must be determined using Method 315 and the performance test submittal must identify the pitch storage tank and control device and any emission points that share the control device.

If the owner or operator demonstrates initial compliance for a pitch storage tank by design evaluation of a carbon adsorber, then the design evaluation must include the affinity of the organic vapors for carbon, amount of carbon in each bed, number of beds, humidity and temperature of the feed gases, flow rate of the organic HAP emission stream, and, if applicable, desorption/regeneration schedule and parameters (including pressure drop for vacuum desorption).

checklist: Confirm that the facility and the specific pitch storage tank are affected sources subject to 40 CFR part 63, Subpart LL.
Record the tank's operational status: date it was idled (March 31, 2016) and the actual or planned restart date (the date that would trigger the 30-day test clock under §63.847(c)(3)(iv)).
Verify whether the facility is an existing source for Subpart LL (i.e., construction/reconstruction dates) and that the October 16, 2017 compliance date for pitch storage tank POM limits applies.

Determine whether the facility is required to obtain/has a Title V (part 70) permit or whether the State of Indiana has delegated authority for extension decisions (to identify whether to submit the extension request to EPA or the State permitting authority).

If seeking an extension, document the date the extension request will be (or was) submitted and whether that is no later than 120 days prior to the October 16, 2017 compliance date, or, if later, document when the need arose and the date the owner first learned of the circumstances (to support a late submission under §63.6(i)(4)(i)(C)).

Prepare the extension request contents: clear description of the carbon adsorber controls to be installed; a compliance schedule with dates for awarding contracts/orders, start of on-site construction/installation, completion of installation, and final compliance; and description of interim measures to minimize emissions during the extension period.

Assemble evidence that additional time is necessary for installation of the carbon adsorber (e.g., procurement lead times, engineering, construction schedule, vendor confirmations) and records demonstrating whether circumstances were beyond the owner's reasonable control (if requesting a late filing).

Decide and document whether initial compliance will be via a design evaluation or a performance test; if design evaluation for carbon adsorber is chosen, prepare documentation covering carbon affinity, amount of carbon per bed, number of beds, feed gas humidity and temperature, flow rates, and regeneration/desorption schedule as required by §63.847(g)(2)(v).

If planning a performance test, confirm capability to perform Method 315 within 30 days after startup (or as soon as practicable) and identify emission points sharing the control device per §63.847(g)(3).
Plan to include any extension conditions in the Title V permit (or request Title V revision) if the source is subject to part 70, per §63.6(i)(4)(i)(A).
